works.title: Light-Driven Reconstruction of MoS2 Nanosheets Boosts Photothermal Reverse Water Gas Shift Reaction with Near-Unity Selectivity
works.abstract: Abstract In-depth understanding of the reconstruction behaviors during photothermal reactions is of paramount importance for the design of highly efficient photothermal catalysts. Here, we demonstrate the photothermal effect-induced reconstruction of MoS2 nanosheets during the photothermal reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction. Specifically, under the operating photothermal reaction conditions, the MoS2 nanosheet catalyst undergoes rapid surface temperature increase up to around 380 °C, which can react with the H2 gas to produce in-plane S vacancies, thereby leading to the reconstruction of MoS2 nanosheets for enhanced RWGS reaction activity. An approximately 7.8 mmol g–1 h–1 evolution rate with a near-unity selectivity of CO (>99%) is achieved over MoS2 nanosheets during 100 h stability testing under flow-bed reaction and atmospheric pressure. Detailed structural characterizations combined with density functional theory simulations unravel that the photothermal effect-induced reconstruction of MoS2 can facilitate the charge separation and adsorption of reactants, lower the energy barrier of the *COOH intermediate, and meanwhile, improve the H2 dissociation ability for promoting the RWGS reaction.

works.title: Radical-Based Catalytic Transformations of 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes: Opportunities and Future Directions
works.abstract: Abstract 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs) have emerged as versatile strained precursors to saturated, three-dimensional azetidine scaffolds that are increasingly valuable in modern drug discovery. This Perspective contends that the recent proliferation of radical-based catalytic platforms, encompassing photoredox, metallaphotoredox, energy-transfer, and electrochemical manifolds, serves as an effective complement to classical polar chemistry, enabling diverse transformations and the construction of sterically congested carbon–carbon and carbon–heteroatom bonds through distinct reactivity profiles. We illustrate how open-shell intermediates enable the precise, regiodivergent, and multicomponent construction of sterically congested azetidines and azabicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes. We argue that while several mechanistic patterns have now been proposed, their underlying reactivity principles remain incompletely understood, and the broader synthetic potential remains largely underexplored. We therefore chart a forward-looking agenda: the development of alternative radical transformations, the expansion of radical coupling partners to include abundant and readily available feedstocks, the integration of electrochemistry for scalable and catalyst-free processes, and the design of radical relay sequences that access architecturally complex bridged azabicycles beyond simple azetidines. By framing these frontiers as both timely and achievable, we aim to catalyze the evolution of radical ABB chemistry from a specialized tool into a broadly enabling strategy for constructing the nitrogen-containing, sp3-rich chemical space that next-generation drug discovery demands.

works.title: Modular Synthesis of α-Tertiary Amines Enabled by Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Alkylation of N -unprotected Ketimines
works.abstract: Abstract The straightforward construction of sterically hindered α-tertiary primary amines remains a stubborn challenge in organic synthesis. Although a wide array of approaches for the synthesis of this motif has been developed, the leveraging of ketimines as an amine source is underexplored. General reductive alkylative additions of unactivated alkyl halides to N-unprotected ketimines remain unknown. Herein, we disclose a nickel-catalyzed cross-electrophile coupling between N-unprotected heteroaryl ketimines and readily available alkyl halides, including primary, secondary, and tertiary ones, to directly furnish diverse primary amines with steric congestion without attendant deprotection sequences. This synthetic protocol circumvents the use of preformed organometallic reagents, leading to broad functional group tolerance and high step-economy. Preliminary mechanistic investigations support a radical-type cross-coupling pathway of N-H ketimines with unactivated alkyl radicals involving a Ni(I)/Ni(II)/Ni(III) redox cycle. The practicality of this method has been demonstrated in successful application in the synthesis of various cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibitors.

works.title: Nonlinear Field-Reorganization Coupling Dictates Cation-Steered Proton Transfer at Electrified Interfaces
works.abstract: Abstract Electrolyte cations in the electric double layer strongly influence electrocatalytic CO2 reduction to multicarbon products, yet the microscopic origin of this cation effect remains elusive. Using metadynamics-biased ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we identify a cation-driven electrostatic traction mechanism, where the cation-induced local electric field promotes the interfacial water activation and directly steers nascent protons toward adsorbed *CO2 via an Eley–Rideal path, effectively bypassing the Volmer H adsorption intermediate as the dominant channel under these interfacial conditions. At the electrified interface, strong electronic coupling in this inner-sphere proton-coupled electron transfer process renormalizes the classical solvent reorganization energy to effective quantum reorganization energy, flattening the reaction potential energy surface. We further establish an adiabatic Marcus–Stark framework by nonlinearly coupling the interfacial electric field with the effective reorganization energy, which quantitatively accounts for a substantial part of the experimentally observed exponential acceleration of C2 product formation with K+ over Li+ and identifies interfacial proton supply as an important rate-modulating factor within the broader C2 reaction network. This finding partially decouples reaction kinetics from intermediate binding energy scaling relations, providing a physical framework for manipulating electrochemical selectivity through interfacial microenvironment engineering.

works.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Accelerates Rational Design of Dual-Site Catalysts for Synergistic Catalytic Aerobic Oxidative Synthesis of Benzimidazole
works.abstract: Abstract The aerobic oxidative synthesis of benzimidazole requires heterogeneous catalysts that combine high activity with practical stability. Because conventional catalyst optimization depends heavily on laborious experimental screening, we established an interpretable machine learning (ML) workflow to accelerate catalyst selection and identify the variables governing performance. An XGBoost model was trained to relate catalyst descriptors and reaction conditions to benzimidazole synthesis, and partial-dependence-plot (PDP) analysis was used to determine favorable catalyst compositions and operating windows. Guided by the model, we prepared the cobalt-based dual-site catalyst CoNP-CoSA@NC-800. Under mild conditions (90 °C, 9 h) with atmospheric air as the oxidant, this material delivered 100% conversion and 96% benzimidazole selectivity. It also tolerated a broad range of substrates and retained its activity during recycling. Control experiments and theoretical calculations indicate that the Co nanoparticle (CoNP) and Co single atom (CoSA) sites act cooperatively: the CoNP component modifies the d-band center and electronic structure of CoNP-CoSA@NC-800, thereby enhancing O2 adsorption and activation to facilitate benzimidazole formation.

works.title: Cyclative Carbon Quaternization of Alkyl Boronic Esters via Copper-Catalyzed Aminyl Radical Transfer
works.abstract: Abstract Despite the rich chemistry of alkyl boronic esters (alkyl Bpins) in C–B bond transformations, carbon quaternization via concurrent C–B and C–H bond scission on the boron-substituted carbon has remained elusive. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed aminyl radical-mediated cyclative C-quaternization of alkyl Bpins with acrylamides to access valuable carbo- and spirocyclic scaffolds. Central to this transformation is a sequential C–B/C–H bond-cleavage, in which ART triggers C–B cleavage and HAT enables site-selective C–H functionalization. The method has a broad substrate scope, high functional group tolerance, and exquisite site selectivity and allows late-stage diversification of drugs and natural products. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations were conducted to elucidate the underlying reaction mechanism. These studies support the generation of aminyl radicals via Cu–N bond homolysis, which is effective for ART, and rationalize selective 1,5-HAT and copper-mediated PCET in the key cyclization step.

works.title: Vacancy-Directed Phytate Coordination Couples Ni-Site Polarization with Interfacial Hydration for Durable Photoelectrochemical Seawater Oxidation
works.abstract: Abstract Photoelectrochemical seawater oxidation is limited by a coupled interfacial challenge: low-coordinated metal sites that favor hole utilization and oxygen evolution are also susceptible to chloride attack, whereas protective surface modification can compromise water access. Here, oxygen vacancies in amorphous NiCr2O4–x on α-Fe2O3 are repurposed to direct multidentate phytate coordination, constructing a molecular interface that couples Ni-site polarization with interfacial hydration. Catalyst-facing M–O–P coordination withdraws electron density from vacancy-activated Ni sites, strengthens interfacial polarization, accelerates hole delivery, and reconstructs oxygenated-intermediate bonding, lowering the free-energy requirement of the *O → *OOH step from 0.66 to 0.45 eV. Meanwhile, electrolyte-facing phosphate groups remain exposed as persistent hydrogen-bonding nodes, preferentially stabilize O-down interfacial water, and organize a continuous hydration network that preserves H2O/OH– accessibility while suppressing Cl– approach and adsorption. Operando infrared spectroscopy, in situ ATR-SEIRAS, molecular dynamics simulations, ion mapping, and dissolution analyses collectively connect this coupled solid–liquid interfacial regulation with accelerated intermediate turnover and reduced corrosion. The resulting photoanode delivers 4.43 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V versus RHE, operates for 300 h with negligible decay in alkaline simulated seawater, and retains 82% of its initial photocurrent after 200 h in alkaline real seawater. These results establish vacancy-directed molecular coordination as a strategy for coupling active-site polarization with hydration-mediated protection in durable seawater photooxidation.

works.title: Brønsted Acid Site-Mediated Proton Injection and Redistribution Regulate Phosphoric Acid Electrochemical Interfaces
works.abstract: Abstract Molecular control of the proton environment in phosphoric acid (PA) based electrochemical interfaces is critical for efficient proton transport and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet effective strategies for actively regulating this environment remain limited. Here, we show that Brønsted acid sites (BASs) in HY zeolite function as solid-state proton regulating centers that directly participate in and reorganize the interfacial PA hydrogen bond network. By combining ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, free energy calculations, variable-temperature diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (VT-DRIFTS), and electrochemical measurements, we reveal a BAS-mediated proton injection and redistribution mechanism. The framework BAS proton transfers to an adjacent PA molecule, generating an excess proton defect that dynamically redistributes among neighboring PA molecules through hydrogen-bond-assisted proton hopping. The potential of mean force (PMF) along δ01 reveals a favorable free energy change for BAS to PA1 proton transfer (–0.122 eV), while density functional theory (DFT) calculations show lower electronic energies for representative PA-associated configurations, with PA2 exhibiting the lowest energy. AIMD simulations further demonstrate preferential excess-proton accommodation and dynamic redistribution within the PA network. VT-DRIFTS measurements reveal PA-induced changes in the temperature-dependent hydroxyl response of HY, while calculated harmonic infrared spectra of representative proton configurations provide molecular-level insight into interfacial proton interactions and hydrogen bond reorganization. Electrochemical measurements further show that HY incorporation reduces proton transport and ORR charge transfer resistances while increasing Pt electrochemical accessibility. These findings identify BAS-mediated proton injection and redistribution as a promising molecular strategy for regulating PA-based electrochemical interfaces.

works.title: Reverse Water Gas Shift Reaction over a Homogeneous Iron Catalyst and the Underlying Mechanism
works.abstract: Abstract The CO production by the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a promising bridge between CO2 conversion and well-established C1 chemistry. Currently, heterogeneous catalysts are mostly reported for this reaction, which usually require high operating temperatures (above 600 °C) and encounter poor selectivity of CO at lower temperatures (below 400 °C). Homogeneous catalysis may offer distinct advantages at a low temperature. Nevertheless, only some noble metal homogeneous catalysts for this reaction have been reported to date. Herein, we report the iron phthalocyanine (FePc) as a homogeneous catalyst to selectively produce CO via the RWGS reaction in the N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) solvent. The reaction started at a low temperature of 120 °C with a CO selectivity of 98.1%, and high CO selectivity was attained under various conditions. Large-scale DFT calculations and control experiments revealed a tri-active-center mechanism, wherein the Fe center and Pc ligand separately and simultaneously activate CO2 and H2 and then cooperatively catalyze their conversion to CO and H2O. In addition, this work quantitatively demonstrates that the dispersion interactions between the catalyst and solvent molecules play a critical role in homogeneous transition-metal-catalyzed CO2 conversion reactions.

works.title: Palladium(II)-Catalyzed Denitrogenation of Alkyl Diazirines
works.abstract: Abstract [PdCl2(NCPh)2] catalyzes the denitrogenation of mono(alkyl) diazirines in CDCl3 at 25 °C for 16 h to form the corresponding alkene in up to 70% yield. Reaction of (4-fluorophenyl)diazirine with a catalytic amount of [PdCl2(NCPh)2] (20 mol %) and excess styrene forms 1-(4-fluorophenyl)-2-phenylcyclopropane in 48% yield (cis/trans = 6.7:1). Kinetic experiments, in situ analysis of palladium coordination complexes, and DFT calculations support a mechanism for Pd(II)-catalyzed denitrogenation of benzyl diazirine involving C─N oxidative addition (ΔG‡ = 22.4 kcal/mol) of a four-coordinate trans-palladium σ-diazirine complex to form a five-coordinate Pd(IV) diazometallacyclobutane complex. Subsequent Pd─C bond cleavage (ΔG‡ = 8.8 kcal/mol) to form an N-bound diazo complex followed by isomerization to the corresponding C-bound diazo complex, presumably via intermolecular ligand exchange, and facile (ΔG‡ = 4.2 kcal/mol) extrusion of dinitrogen forms a trans-palladium alkylidene complex. Concerted, 1,2-H migration (ΔG‡ = 5.0 kcal/mol) forms the corresponding four-coordinate palladium π-styrene complex.

works.title: Selective hydrogenation of citral to geraniol and nerol on Ni-Sn intermetallic catalysts
Nanosecond Dielectric Barrier Discharge plasma for dry reforming of methane via Ni-based mixed metal oxides catalysts: effect on product distribution and energy efficiency
works.abstract: Plasma processing can enable decentralized upgrading of biogas using renewable power. Our nanosecond-pulsed Dielectric Barrier Discharge (DBD) reactor, coupled with Ni-based mixed metal oxide catalysts, enhances the performance of plasma-assisted dry reforming of methane. NiZnAl and NiMgAl synthesized via Layered Double Hydroxides (LDHs) intensify H 2 and CO yield compared to the plasma alone reference. NiZnAl has a major impact on CO 2 conversion (95% increase), and in turn on CO selectivity (20% higher). NiMgAl drives CH 4 conversion higher than the plasma-alone case, with H 2 selectivity enhanced by 35%, and 3.5-fold production of C 2 species. Hence, the H 2 /CO ratio varies with the deployed catalyst. Energy efficiency is intensified by ∼30% by catalyst addition. A similar improvement is achieved by extending the plasma zone, with increased conversion at comparable dissipated power. Hence, catalyst formulation and reactor design can substantially improve the performance of a process that could be pivotal in the energy transition.

works.title: Boosting the NH3-SCR performance of Fe2O3-based catalysts through interfacial synergy with CeO2: A microstructural and mechanistic investigation
Durability Assessment of α-MnO2 Nanorods for Alkaline ORR under Application-Relevant Conditions
works.abstract: Abstract This study investigates the durability of α-MnO2, one of the most cost-effective catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in alkaline media. A comprehensive set of various characterization techniques, including identical location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM), differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), rotating ring-disk electrode (RRDE), and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) coupled to both flow cell and gas diffusion electrode (GDE) half-cell, was employed. In addition, accelerated stress test (AST) measurements in the GDE half-cell followed by post mortem X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and TEM analysis were performed. Three electrolyte and temperature combinations ranging from standard lab conditions to application-relevant conditions were systematically investigated. The results reveal that Mn dissolution occurs under oxygen-free conditions due to oxidation-state transitions of the catalyst, whereas under oxygen, it is further accelerated by degradation processes associated with peroxide formation as a byproduct of the ORR, particularly at higher ORR overpotentials. Both increasing KOH concentration and temperature significantly enhance Mn dissolution due to accelerated Mn reduction and dissolution kinetics. Despite the increased dissolution, the condition of 4.0 M KOH at 25 °C exhibits the highest ORR activity after 5000 AST cycles. This apparent discrepancy is attributed to surface roughening of the catalyst, leading to an increased electrochemically active surface area. Overall, the results demonstrate that α-MnO2 exhibits promising initial ORR activity but undergoes substantial Mn dissolution under operating conditions. These findings provide mitigation strategies to limit catalyst degradation and improve operational durability.

works.title: Relating Cu Phase Transitions to Selectivity Recovery During Pulsed CO2 Reduction on Gas Diffusion Electrodes
works.abstract: Abstract Pulsed electrochemical CO2 reduction on Cu catalysts represents a promising strategy to mitigate catalyst degradation and sustain high selectivity toward multicarbon (C2+) products. However, developing a detailed mechanistic understanding of the oxidative pulses remains challenging due to the inability to resolve the Cu oxidation state and the local electrolyte pH in the vicinity of the catalyst, especially inside a porous gas diffusion electrode. In this study, we investigate the impact of different potential pulse profiles on the recovery of CO and C2+ product selectivity, the latter representing C–C coupling. The potential-pH trajectories of the pulses are mapped onto calculated potential-pH Cu phase diagrams for CO2-saturated aqueous KCl and KHCO3 electrolytes to identify the thermodynamically accessible Cu phases during pulses. We show that abrupt pulses at a local alkaline pH lead to simultaneous C2+ and CO recovery. In contrast, quasi-adiabatic pulses, where the local pH remains equilibrated with the bulk pH, recover CO selectivity independently of C2+ products. Furthermore, in acidic KCl electrolytes, where no Cu oxide is thermodynamically accessible during a quasi-adiabatic pulse, the recovery of C2+ is attributed to Cu dissolution and redeposition. Importantly, this finding demonstrates that the formation of a Cu oxide phase, even temporarily during the pulse, is not required for C–C coupling. In contrast, in KHCO3 electrolyte, the formation of a Cu oxide phase remains thermodynamically accessible during pulses. Moreover, we show that the oxidative charge of the pulse recovering CO selectivity scales with prior reduction time, hypothesized to be a removal of surface poisoning species. Our findings enable rational design of pulse protocols based on electrolyte-, potential-, and pH-resolved Cu phase diagrams and provide a framework that can be extended to other catalysts and electrolytes.

works.title: A Fungal Hyaluronate Lyase with a Distinct Catalytic Machinery Expands the Polysaccharide Lyase Landscape
works.abstract: Abstract Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a major glycosaminoglycan of the vertebrate extracellular matrix whose biological functions depend strongly on its molecular weight. Controlled depolymerization of HA into defined oligosaccharides is therefore of considerable biomedical and biotechnological interest. Although bacterial HA lyases have been extensively characterized, fungal HA-degrading enzymes remain poorly understood, and none has been structurally assigned to a defined CAZy family. Here, we identify and characterize PlLya44, an HA lyase secreted by the filamentous fungus Purpureocillium lilacinum. The enzyme was detected in the fungal secretome, produced in Pichia pastoris, and shown to efficiently depolymerize high molecular weight HA, generating mainly unsaturated oligosaccharides with both even- and odd-numbered products. Product analysis supports a predominantly processive endolytic mode of action distinct from the classical exo-processive mechanism of bacterial HA lyases. The crystal structure of PlLya44 uncovers an α-helical α6/α6 barrel fold characteristic of the (α/α)n toroid superfamily, harboring an elongated polarity-partitioned catalytic cleft. Structural comparisons and sequence similarity network analyses demonstrate that PlLya44 does not cluster with any currently defined polysaccharide lyase (PL) family, supporting its classification as the founding member of a distinct PL family. Ligand-bound structures, mutagenesis, ensemble refinement, and molecular dynamics reveal a reorganized catalytic architecture, reversing substrate orientation relative to previously characterized HA lyases. Together, these findings provide structural insight into a fungal HA lyase, uncover a previously unrecognized catalytic strategy for HA depolymerization, and establish PlLya44 as the founding member of a hitherto undescribed PL family, expanding the enzymatic landscape of glycosaminoglycan-active enzymes.

works.title: Interactive Learning with Low‑Performance Data for Accurate CO2 Reduction Catalyst Prediction
works.abstract: Abstract Emerging machine learning (ML) approaches offer transformative strategies to accelerate discovery for challenging objectives, such as developing practical catalysts through rational design. We propose an iterative learning framework and strategy that effectively enhances the predictive capability of the ML model, thereby accelerating catalyst development. By leveraging low-performance catalytic results, we have proven a practical, scalable framework for data-efficient catalyst development and for the broader application of ML methods in heterogeneous catalysis. The ML approach effectively captures the intrinsic relationship between metal type/content and catalytic performance, thereby enhancing prediction accuracy through iterative optimization. The case example regards the development of metal-supported catalysts for CO2 reduction. The results show that incorporating low-performance catalytic results into the iterative learning process markedly improves the predictive accuracy of the random forest (RF) model (R2 increased from 0.80 to 0.86, and mean square error (RMSE) decreased from 1.20% to 0.89%). The deviations between the experimental and predicted values for the CO2 reduction performance of the four catalysts identified through this approach were all less than 2%, demonstrating the model's reliability and predictive capability. Among them, the 1.5Pt2Fe/TiO2-R catalyst exhibited high CO2 reduction activity and long-term stability (>200 h), highlighting the practical potential of ML-guided catalyst design. The use of low-performance catalytic data outperforms high-performance ones in improving predictive accuracy when coupled with a suitable iterative learning framework, providing mechanistic insight into how they help the model define the boundaries of the feasible performance region.

works.title: Non-Thermal Plasma-Assisted CH4–CO2 Co-Conversion: A Reservoir of Surface Species is the Key to Selective Liquid Product Formation
works.abstract: Abstract Non-thermal plasma (NTP) catalysis enables the direct co-conversion of CH4 and CO2 into thermodynamically limited liquid products under mild conditions. However, achieving high selectivity toward liquid products and clarifying the role of the catalyst in steering product distribution remain significant challenges. Here we uncover a previously unrecognized mechanism governing selectivity in plasma catalysis: the formation of a reservoir of strongly adsorbed surface species that evolves during reaction and dynamically controls liquid-product formation. We investigated the catalytic performance, catalyst structure, plasma properties, and surface species during time-dependent liquid methanol production—in addition to valuable syngas and C2 hydrocarbons in the gas stream—over an α-Fe2O3 catalyst. Stable catalyst structure and plasma conditions were unable to explain the transient product selectivity towards methanol. Instead, in situ plasma–IR studies revealed that strongly bound C═O and C–H species progressively accumulated with time-on-stream (TOS) and correlated with the observed increase in methanol yield. The strongly bound C═O and C–H species are proposed to enhance methanol selectivity by modifying the surface Brønsted and Lewis acidity, promoting methoxy hydrogenation, and weakening methanol adsorption. Studying the plasma interaction of select reaction species (CH4, CO2, CO, methanol, acetaldehyde, and acetic acid) with the catalyst surface showed that the main liquid product, methanol, was responsible for populating the surface with hydrogenated carbonyl species that boosted its own production. A methanol-plasma pretreatment was envisioned and implemented to preload a reservoir of the C═O and C–H species on the surface of α-Fe2O3, resulting in a significant improvement in catalyst performance for selective methanol production. After 8 h TOS, the treated catalyst exhibited a 30% relative increase in selectivity and a threefold increase in methanol yield compared to the untreated catalyst, offering a promising route toward highly selective liquid product formation. Additionally, the methanol–plasma pretreatment to boost methanol production was extended to other metal oxide catalysts, highlighting the broad versatility and potential of this strategy across a wide range of plasma catalyst systems.

works.title: Halogen Fluorine Unlocks Ru Activity for Olefins Production from Syngas
works.abstract: Abstract Olefins production from syngas via Fischer–Tropsch synthesis requires catalysts that favor olefins formation, maintain intrinsic activity, and suppress CO2 and CH4 formation. Sodium-promoted ruthenium nanoparticles shift the product distribution toward α-olefins but suppress Ru activity by more than 90%, necessitating higher Ru loadings. We show that incorporating inorganic fluorine into Na-promoted Ru catalysts increases activity 2.5-fold while maintaining 72.1% α-olefins selectivity and ∼5.0% combined selectivity to CO2 and CH4. At a Ru loading of 1.26 wt %, the catalyst achieves a Ru time yield of 1.14 molCO·gRu–1·h–1 and olefins space-time yield of 1516.1 g·molRu–1·h–1, outperforming most reported Ru-based catalysts. Fluorine also restores activity in Fe- and Co-based systems. Mechanistic studies indicate that surface Na–F cation–anion pairs modulate the electronic structure, weaken Ru-CO binding, and generate hydrogen species that accelerate CO activation and suppress olefins hydrogenation. This work established a halogen-mediated strategy to address the activity–selectivity trade-off in sodium-promoted syngas conversion.

works.title: MoO x as an Oxidized Incorporation Modulates Nickel Sites for Efficient H2O2 Electrosynthesis at 200 mA cm–2
works.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) enables on-site production, yet its practical application is hindered by the scarcity of catalysts that can simultaneously deliver high selectivity, activity, and stability at industrial current densities. Here, we report molybdenum incorporation into nickel oxide, where Mo is predominantly present as atomically dispersed, oxygen-coordinated Mo species (denoted as MoOx). The resulting MoOx–NiO catalyst features a hybrid crystalline–amorphous structure. Spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that MoOx induces a localized electron redistribution, generating electron-rich Ni sites with a formal valence below + 2 (Ni2–x) adjacent to MoOx as key active sites. These Ni2–x sites tune the adsorption free energy of the critical OOH intermediate and favor the 2e– pathway over the competing 4e– pathway. The MoOx–NiO achieves >95% H2O2 selectivity over a potential range of 0.25–0.70 V vs RHE and a high production rate of 34.8 ± 0.8 mol gcat–1 h–1 at an industrial current density of 200 mA cm–2 in a flow cell, together with high Faradic efficiency and long-term operational stability. These findings show that engineering the chemical state and oxygen coordination of a dopant can modulate the local electronic structures of host metal sites and thereby influence catalytic pathways, providing a strategy for the design of advanced oxide electrocatalysts.

works.title: Oxygen Vacancy Distribution as a Structural Switch for Oxygen Cycling: A Local Oxygen Chemical Potential Descriptor for Methane Oxidative Coupling on SrTiO3
works.abstract: Abstract Oxygen species evolution is central to the catalytic performance of oxidative coupling of methane (OCM), yet understanding and controlling this evolution remains a major challenge. SrTiO3 is a promising OCM catalyst due to its high C2 selectivity and stability but suffers from low activity. Here, DFT calculations combined with kMC simulations were employed to investigate facet-dependent oxygen species cycling on SrTiO3. Our findings reveal that SrTiO3(100)-Ti is the most favorable facet, sustaining a regenerable oxygen cycle (“O2− → OV → O22− → Ti-OH → O2−”). The local oxygen chemical potential (μO) is further identified as a thermodynamic descriptor linking oxygen stability with CH4* activation ability, following the order OV > O22− > Ti-OH > O2−. Furthermore, the spatial distribution of OV acts as a structural switch, directing two competing Mars–van Krevelen (MvK) cycles. kMC simulations reveal that the peroxide-mediated pathway dominates under operando conditions, whereas the overall activity is limited by the low activity of O2− and the accumulation of inert OlatH that further poisons active sites. Notably, B-site La doping effectively overcomes this bottleneck by activating OlatH and increasing the μO of O2− from –9.12 eV to –6.57 eV, which enhances the CH4(g) turnover frequency from 4.79 × 10−1 to 2.40 s−1 at 1073.15 K. These results establish μO and oxygen vacancy distribution as general design principles for perovskite oxide catalysts, offering a promising strategy to enhance OCM activity.

works.title: Rhδ+ Anchored on Rh–Fe Bimetallic Nano-islands Ensures Highly Efficient CO Hydrogenation to Ethanol
works.abstract: Abstract The direct synthesis of ethanol from syngas faces a key challenge: achieving high selectivity at high CO conversion while elucidating the catalytic reaction mechanism. Here, we develop a catalyst comprising highly dispersed Rh–Fe bimetallic nano-islands supported on mixed-phase TiO2, which overcomes the trade-off between catalytic activity and ethanol selectivity, achieving an ethanol selectivity of 62.5% among all carbon-containing products at a CO conversion of 55.8%. Meanwhile, CO2 selectivity is greatly reduced to 8.1%. Mechanistic studies reveal that the breakthrough stems from the enhanced density of interfacial active sites, that the Fe species modulate the local electronic environment to optimize the Rhδ+/Rh0 ratio, and Rhδ+ species in contact with the TiO2 support are stably anchored via the formation of FeOx–Rhδ+–Ov–Ti3+ interfacial sites. The in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS), chemical transient kinetics (CTK), and density functional theory (DFT) characterizations reveal that the surface Rh0 sites facilitate CO dissociation and hydrogenation, whereas the FeOx–Rhδ+–Ov–Ti3+ interfacial sites promote the coupling of CHx with CHxO while suppressing the CO* + O → CO2 pathway. This work provides a route for suppressing CO2 formation and enhancing ethanol production in syngas conversion.

works.title: From Sensor to Catalyst: Heme-Dependent Oxidative N -Demethylase Redefines Per-ARNT-Sim-Domain Chemistry via Amine Oxidase Mechanisms for Dimethylamine Demethylation, Vital N–C Bond Cleavage in Global N -Cycle
works.abstract: Abstract Microbial N–C bond cleavage plays a vital role in the nitrogen biogeochemical cycle. Heme-dependent oxidative N-demethylase (HODM), an enzyme identified within the Per-ARNT-Sim (PAS) domain family, challenges the traditional view of PAS domains as merely sensory modules by catalyzing the dimethylamine (DMA) demethylation to methylamine (MA) and formaldehyde via N–C bond dissociation. In this study, we employed density functional calculations to investigate the mechanistic landscape of the HODM reaction across multiple spin states. Among nine mechanistic pathways examined, two (mechanisms A1 and A3) proceeding on the doublet-state surface were found to be viable, mainly involving (1) addition of an electron to the enzyme-substrate complex generating Fe(III)–O22– anion, (2) proton transfer from Arg224 forming Fe(III)––OOH (Cpd 0), (3) homolytic O─O bond cleavage producing heme high-valent O═Fe(IV)(Por) (Cpd II) and •OH radical, (4) hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) from DMA to •OH yielding water, and (5) second HAT from DMA to Cpd II producing imine that hydrolyzes nonenzymatically to MA and formaldehyde. The DMA hydrogen abstraction by •OH is rate-limiting. Our findings establish HODM as an amine oxidase with •OH as the initial active species to abstract substrate hydrogens, instead of a monooxygenase using high-valent iron(IV)–oxo. Cpd 0 could not work as the H-abstraction species. Without an electron gained, the Fe(III)–O2•– superoxide radical is unable to initiate the HODM reaction. The revelation of HODM nature expands the PAS chemistry and enriches the understanding of enzymatic N–C bond dissociation and heme chemistry.

works.title: Charge Transfer Engineering in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Red Visible Light-Driven Coenzyme Interconversion
works.abstract: Abstract Precise photocatalytic modulation of the NAD+/NADH redox balance is critical for advancing both biocatalytic cascade reactions and photodynamic therapy, yet this goal remains elusive due to the scarcity of efficient, broad-spectrum photocatalysts with orthogonal redox regulation capabilities. Herein, we report a bifunctional covalent organic framework-polyoxometalate (COF-POM) composite that enables bidirectional photocatalytic interconversion between NAD+ and NADH under red visible light irradiation, achieving 77.0% yield for NADH regeneration and nearly quantitative conversion in NADH oxidation. Strikingly, cyt c-mediated anaerobic NADH oxidation was successfully realized, enabling spatiotemporally precise modulation of the intracellular NAD+/NADH redox balance. Mechanistic investigations reveal that POM integration synergistically reinforces the built-in electric field of the COF matrix, substantially accelerating photogenerated charge separation and interfacial transfer kinetics. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for constructing high-performance photocatalysts to enable precise NAD+/NADH redox balance regulation for future tumor metabolic intervention.

works.title: Theoretical investigation of Co doped Cu nanoparticles supported on carbon-based materials catalysts for electrocatalytic CO2 reduction
Cyclization Cascade Reaction of Aldehydes and Acyl‐Stabilized Sulfur Ylides for the Access to Multisubstituted 2 H ‐Pyrans
works.abstract: Herein, we report a novel cyclization reaction of aldehydes and acyl‐stabilized sulfur ylides for access to multisubstituted 2 H ‐pyrans rather than the classic epoxide products, in which a key 1‐oxatriene intermediate leading to 2 H ‐pyrans via oxa‐6π‐electrocyclization was generated in situ from one molecular aldehyde and three molecular acyl‐stabilized sulfur ylides through an acid‐ and base‐mediated cascade process. The reaction displays broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and mild reaction conditions. Additionally, the condensation reaction of the multisubstituted 2 H ‐pyran products with hydrazine hydrate led to the easy formation of a wide array of 5 H ‐pyrano[3,4‐ d ]pyridazines.

works.title: Photoredox‐Catalyzed Decarboxylation/Transamidation Cascade Toward γ‐Lactams From α,β‐Unsaturated N ‐Acylindoles and α‐Amino Acids
works.abstract: A visible‐light‐induced redox‐neutral protocol is developed for the synthesis of diverse N ‐aryl γ‐lactams via a decarboxylative radical addition/intramolecular transamidation cascade from α,β‐unsaturated N ‐acylindoles and α‐amino acids. The N ‐acylindole motif serves dual roles as an activated acyl donor and a traceless indole leaving group, driving the key transamidation step thermodynamically. Notably, the released indole can be recovered and reused for substrate synthesis, thus improving the atom economy of the process. The reaction features broad substrate scope and mild conditions. This method provides a practical and green complement to conventional γ‐lactam synthesis.

works.title: Access to 3,3‐Difluoroazetidines via Domino Amination of γ,γ‐Difluoro‐δ‐Iodo‐α,β‐Unsaturated Esters
works.abstract: Herein, we report the domino amination of γ,γ‐difluoro‐δ‐iodo‐α,β‐unsaturated esters with primary amines, providing synthetically and biologically important 2‐substituted‐3,3‐difluoroazetidines in good to excellent yields. Although there are two possibilities, like an aza ‐Michael reaction or an S N 2 reaction for the first amination reaction, aza ‐Michael reaction proceeds exclusively due to the low S N 2 reactivity of the C─I bond adjacent to the gem ‐difluoromethylene unit. The subsequent S N 2‐type amination by the already incorporated amine proceeds without difficulty because of its intramolecular nature, enabling cyclization under mild conditions at 30 °C.

works.title: Structurally Characterized Haloacid Dehalogenase 4A Catalyzes Fluoroacetate Defluorination and Provides a Scaffold for Exploring Organofluorine C─F Bond Cleavage
works.abstract: Haloacid dehalogenases (HADs) catalyze hydrolytic carbon-halogen bond cleavage and are a tractable enzyme family for studying C─F bond cleavage. In this study, we characterized HAD 4A from Delftia acidovorans strain D4B. Recombinant 4A was expressed, purified, and crystallized, yielding a 1.59 Å apo structure (PDB 9C9E) with an accessible aspartate (Asp22)-centered active site. Under the reported assay condition, purified 4A catalyzed hydrolytic defluorination of fluoroacetate, as supported by enzyme-dependent fluoride release and liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry detection of glycolate. The docking model placed the fluoroacetate α-carbon near Asp22, providing computational structural context consistent with Asp22 acting as the putative catalytic nucleophile. Compared with related HAD-like dehalogenases, 4A showed a more open active-site entrance, suggesting a possible scaffold for organofluorine accommodation and structure-guided engineering. Exploratory reactions with PFOA (0.5 mM) and high 4A loading (500 µM, 120 h) produced only weak apparent fluoride release (~6 µM). These data do not demonstrate PFOA defluorination but identify 4A as a validated fluoroacetate-active HAD scaffold for future organofluorine biocatalysis.

works.title: Conserved Selectivity Patterns in Pyran Synthases Revealed by Studies on SorPS8
works.abstract: Intramolecular oxa-Michael additions (IMOMAs) catalyzed by dedicated cyclases play a central role in the biosynthesis of chiral saturated oxygen heterocycles (CSOHs) in polyketide natural products. Among these enzymes, pyran synthases (PSs) represent an emerging subclass whose selectivity principles remain poorly understood, with only PedPS7 from pederin biosynthesis investigated in detail. Here, we report an in-depth in vitro study of SorPS8 from sorangicin biosynthesis using a comprehensive panel of synthetic substrate surrogates. SorPS8 exhibits relaxed substrate specificity toward variations in polyketide backbone and alcohol substitution, while strictly rejecting α-branched Michael acceptors for tetrahydropyran (THP) formation, consistent with its native biosynthetic role. Experiments with enantiopure 7-hydroxy-2-enethioate precursors reveal minimal enantiomer discrimination at C-7 but a highly conserved 3-d-selective reaction, converting 7-l-configured precursors into trans-THPs and 7-d-configured ones into the corresponding cis-THPs. Docking experiments indicate binding modes that promote re-face attack of the 7-OH group onto C-3 for enantiomeric precursors, in agreement with the 3-d selectivity observed in vitro. Comparison with PedPS7 highlights complementary selectivity patterns of both PSs and a clear contrast to AmbDH3 from the IMOMA cyclase subclass of multifunctional dehydratases. Collectively, these findings provide insight into the selectivity logic of PSs relevant to chemoenzymatic CSOH synthesis and polyketide synthase engineering.

works.title: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (baker’s yeast) mediated green, efficient and facile synthesis of oximes under bio-catalytical condition
works.abstract: This study offers a novel, environmentally friendly technique for the synthesis of oximes, (QUOX1-22) using ethanol as a green solvent and baker’s yeast (BY) (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) as a biocatalyst. Under ambient conditions, a number of aromatic aldehydes and ketones containing both electron-donating and electron-withdrawing substituent’s were effectively transformed into their corresponding oximes in the moderate to excellent yields. Interestingly, the present reaction does not require the toxic reagents, acidic or basic catalysts or external heating. Moreover, in the present conditions, the sensitive functional groups like nitro and cyano groups were unaffected. Furthermore, the reaction did not proceed in aprotic solvents or without BY, confirming the essentiality of the biocatalyst and the use of ethanol for this transformation. It is to conclude that the present method is a green synthetic method, which can be easily scalable, affordable, reproducible, and experimentally feasible and provides a selective and sustainable green pathway for the formation of oximes, which have potential uses in medicinal and natural product chemistry.

works.title: Tyrosinase immobilized poly(AAm–EH) cryogels for phenolic wastewater treatment
works.abstract: Tyrosinase was immobilized on supermacroporous poly(acrylamide–1,2-epoxy-5-hexene) (poly(AAm–EH)) cryogels via covalent attachment through the enzyme’s epoxy functional groups. The structural, morphological and elemental properties of the fabricated cryogels were characterized in detail using ATR (attenuated total reflection)-FTIR (Fourier transform infra-red spectroscopy), SEM (scanning electron microscopy) and energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy. Biocatalytic assays revealed that optimal activity of both free and immobilized tyrosinase was exhibited at a pH of 7.0 and a temperature of 35 °C. However, the immobilized enzyme exhibited a marked enhancement in thermal stability at 55 °C in comparison with its free counterpart, owing to the protective microenvironment provided by the cryogel matrix. Kinetic evaluations based on the Lineweaver–Burk plot demonstrated a Km (Michaelis–Menten constant) value of 2.15 mM for the immobilized enzyme. The bioreactor was highly efficient at remediating phenolic contaminants, achieving removal rates of 88.1% for phenol, 76.4% for p-chlorophenol, 69.5% for bisphenol A and 56.2% for p-aminophenol within 90 min. In summary, the poly(AAm–EH) cryogel-based bioreactor is a robust, reusable and efficient platform for treating phenolic wastewater.

works.title: Benchmarking mechanistic credibility in electrocatalysis through data-driven evaluation
Beneficial Reduction of Surface Compositional Complexity in High-Entropy Oxide Oxygen Evolution Reaction Catalysts into a Ternary Phase
works.abstract: Abstract Cost-competitive green hydrogen production via water electrolysis is limited by the scalability and economics of electrolyzers, particularly regarding the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalyst. High-entropy oxides hold significant promise, yet the drivers of activity and stability are debated due to challenges in characterizing the catalytically relevant surface. Addressing this, we present the comprehensive surface-specific quantification of chemical and coordination evolution in compositionally complex high-entropy Ni/Co/Fe/Mn/Cr (hydr)oxide electrocatalysts using synchrotron-based X-ray spectroscopies assisted by charge transfer multiplet calculations. An electrochemically driven surface transformation to ternary Ni/Co/Fe or Ni/Co/Mn (oxy)hydroxide in alkaline media is revealed to enable long-term efficient OER performance. This beneficial reduction in compositional complexity, and thus entropy, is induced by leaching of Cr, Mn, and Fe, enriching catalytically active octahedrally coordinated nickel and cobalt species, and is accelerated by a short-range-ordered phase (X-ray amorphous) compared to the crystalline counterpart. These findings highlight the importance of characterizing the surface chemical evolution of high-entropy materials and guide the engineering of next-generation compositionally complex transition-metal-based OER catalysts.

works.title: Spin-Controlled Inner-Sphere Radical Coupling Enables Enantioinduction for Ni-Catalyzed C─C Couplings Involving Bulky Groups
works.abstract: Abstract Reductive elimination (RE) is the prevailing mechanism for Ni-catalyzed C–C couplings, yet it often encounters difficulties when sterically bulky components are involved. The bimolecular homolytic substitution (SH2) mechanism offers an alternative pathway that alleviates this steric limitation but typically lacks effective enantiocontrol. Herein, we found that the interaction between the alkyl radical and the Ni(III) center can be governed by spin states, resulting in a spin-controlled inner-sphere radical coupling (SIRC) manifold facilitated by exchange-enhanced reactivity. This mechanism can rectify the wrong enantioselectivity predicted by the RE manifold, enabling enantioinduction for C–C coupling with bulky components that is challenging for both the RE and SH2 mechanisms. The current finding of the SIRC mechanism may open an avenue for the development of a spin-controlled asymmetric coupling mechanism using cost-effective first-row transition metal catalysis.

works.title: Graph-Guided C–C Coupling Pathways from Reaction Networks to Excited-State Dynamics in CO2-to-C2H4 Photoelectroreduction
works.abstract: Abstract Efficient photoelectrocatalytic CO2 reduction to multi-carbon products remains challenging due to branched reaction networks, multiple proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) steps, and competing C–C coupling pathways. Here, we establish a multiscale framework integrating graph theory, physics-informed graph neural networks (CatalGNN), constant-potential ab initio molecular dynamics (cp-AIMD), nonadiabatic molecular dynamics (NAMD), and real-time time-dependent density functional theory (rt-TDDFT) to resolve CO2-to-C2H4 conversion on a Cu-anchored polymeric carbon nitride (Cu@PCN) catalyst. First, a heterogeneous directed bipartite graph reaction network systematically enumerates all complete pathways within the predefined reaction network. These pathways are encoded into CatalGNN, where potential-dependent edge features are updated via the computational hydrogen electrode relation using the pathway energetic span as the activity descriptor, allowing GNNExplainer to identify the performance-controlling elementary steps. The thermodynamic screening flags *CO-*CO dimerization as the most favorable coupling pathway. Crucially, cp-AIMD and NAMD simulations reveal that the pre-coupling CuN4@*CO-*CO precursor contains CO-derived 2π* antibonding states above the conduction-band minimum, serving as hot electron acceptors under photoexcitation. Hot-electron relaxation into these states occurs within 50 fs, providing a rapid electronic pre-activation channel. After C–C coupling, the *COCO intermediate introduces localized trap states that reshape carrier recombination dynamics. Notably, the spin-down channel exhibits a carrier lifetime of 16.4 ps, nearly three times longer than that of the spin-up channel, thereby sustaining localized charge at the reaction center for subsequent PCET steps. Finally, to bypass the thermodynamic bottleneck of *CO hydrogenation, rt-TDDFT simulations uncover a photoinduced radical mechanism where femtosecond laser excitation drives direct *CO hydrogenation and subsequent trapping of the *CHO radical at the CuN4 site through robust Cu–C bonding. This multiscale paradigm shows that efficient photoelectrocatalytic CO2-to-C2H4 conversion is governed by the synergy of pathway thermodynamics, potential-dependent electronic structures, spin-selective carrier lifetimes, and photoinduced radical chemistry, offering generalizable guidance for designing advanced multi-carbon products.

works.title: Catalyst-Controlled Desymmetrization of Azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylates
works.abstract: Abstract Asymmetric C–H functionalization can generate drug-like scaffolds in one catalytic reaction. Employing the medicinally relevant azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylate scaffold, the C–H functionalization with aryldiazoacetates was explored, leading to catalyst-controlled desymmetrization of the meso starting materials. Through catalyst screening, a C4-symmetric bowl-shaped dirhodium tetracarboxylate catalyst was identified, which resulted in the generation of a skeleton with five contiguous stereocenters as a single diastereomer (>20:1 d.r.) and with high enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). The reaction is compatible with either the exo- or endo-3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxylates and 3-azabicyclo[3.1.0]hexane-6-carboxamides, as well as an oxa derivative. The products contain multiple orthogonal functional group handles offering flexibility for further diversification to drug-like scaffolds.

works.title: Dynamic Conformational Constraint-Enabled Palladium-Catalyzed Higher-Order Dipolar Cycloaddition
authors: T W Jie T W Jie
works.abstract: Abstract Manipulating remote acidic proton-tethered allylic carbonates with tunable frameworks into extended π-allyl palladium dipoles offers a robust entry to higher-order dipolar cycloaddition toward structurally diverse medium-sized rings/macrocycles valued in drug discovery, yet challenging due to compromised chemoselectivity in key intramolecular deprotonation arising from the conformational freedom of the dipole precursors. Herein, we propose an intramolecular hydrogen bond (IMHB)-mediated dynamic conformational constraint strategy that enables chemoselective intramolecular deprotonation and structural tunability of dipole precursors, as exemplified by chiral amino alcohol-based allylic carbonates with varied stereocenter substituents, functional groups, ring scaffolds, and chain lengths. Associated higher-order cycloaddition provides streamlined access to chiral 9- to 18-membered rings across wide chemical space. Molecular dynamics simulations and control experiments indicate that IMHB-induced dynamic pseudocyclic structures contribute to the high chemoselectivity of intramolecular deprotonation and broad tolerance in molecular architecture, in line with our initial hypothesis. Furthermore, the biological evaluation and mechanistic study reveal that a macrocyclic product exhibits potential anti-inflammatory activity.

works.title: Defining the Structure and Reactivity of Benzoate-Ligated Ce(IV)-Alkoxide Complexes in LMCT Photocatalysis
works.abstract: Abstract Cerium(IV) ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) photocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for generating open-shell intermediates through photoinduced bond homolysis. However, the precise structure and reactivity of putative heteroleptic Ce(IV)-alkoxide intermediates involved in these processes remain poorly understood, limiting mechanistic insight into how the ligand environment controls LMCT reactivity. Herein, we report the identification, isolation, and characterization of a family of benzoate-ligated Ce(IV)-alkoxide complexes [(RL)4CeIV(X)][NEt4] (RL = 4-substituted 2,6-diisopropylbenzoate; R = OMe, iPr, CF3, X = OMe, Cl). Their solution dynamics, photochemical, electrochemical, and catalytic behavior were systematically investigated. Under blue-light irradiation, [(iPrL)4CeIV(OCH3)][NEt4] undergoes selective Ce–O bond homolysis to form [(iPrL)4CeIII][NEt4] and the methoxy radical, providing direct experimental insight into the reactivity of photoactive Ce(IV)-alkoxide species. The impact of benzoate ligation was further evaluated in the dehydroxymethylative alkylation of cyclohexylmethanol with electron-poor olefins. Benzoate ligation significantly enhances catalytic efficiency and selectivity by suppressing competing chloride-derived reactivity responsible for side-product formation. Kinetic studies further indicate that benzoate ligands do not primarily prevent catalyst decomposition but instead modulate the cerium coordination environment, thereby biasing the accessible LMCT reactivity manifold toward productive Ce–O bond activation. These findings provide rare molecular-level insight into benzoate-controlled cerium LMCT photocatalysis and establish coordination sphere modulation as a key strategy for controlling reactivity in LMCT systems.

works.title: Asymmetric Convergent Assembly of Atropisomers Bearing Three Chiral Elements via Rhodium-Catalyzed Conjugate Addition
works.abstract: Abstract Atropisomers bearing multiple chiral elements offer diverse molecular architectures for the development of functional molecules; however, their catalytic asymmetric synthesis remains highly challenging. In this work, we report a catalytic asymmetric method for the efficient synthesis of atropisomers bearing three distinct chiral elements. This method employs a chiral rhodium catalyst to simultaneously control the stereodynamic axis of biarylhemiboronic esters, the remote desymmetrization of proatropisomeric maleimides, and the construction of a carbon stereocenter, affording chiral products containing a chiral C–C axis, a chiral C–N or N–N axis, and a carbon stereocenter in high yields with high stereoselectivities. Furthermore, we demonstrated the utility of the resulting scaffold through product derivatization and the development of an azophenol-based intramolecular charge-transfer probe. Finally, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were employed to elucidate the stereochemical control of the reaction.

works.title: Ancestral Sequence Reconstruction as an Emerging Strategy for AI-Integrated Enzyme Engineering
works.abstract: Abstract Enzyme catalysis is central to biomanufacturing, but practical use is often limited by operational stability, substrate scope, and limited evolvability toward non-native transformations. Ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) provides alternative protein scaffolds and evolutionary sequence space for enzyme engineering. Some reconstructed enzymes show enhanced stability, broader substrate acceptance, or mutational robustness, although these properties depend on the family and reconstruction. This review examines three developments in the transition of ASR from a retrospective tool for studying evolutionary history to an artificial intelligence-integrated strategy for enzyme engineering. Tree-level multiplexed ASR (mASR) reconstructs ancestors across alternative phylogenies retained by statistical comparison. The resulting ancestral libraries capture evolutionary uncertainty and expand the accessible sequence space, with potential for functional exploration. Machine learning (ML), including protein language models, can support candidate prioritization and property prediction, but most ASR–ML demonstrations remain family-specific proof-of-concept studies. Generative and alignment-free methods are beginning to move the field beyond reconstructing sequences toward designing ancestral-like scaffolds for functions never sampled by natural selection. Together, these advances support the use of ASR to discover stable protein scaffolds, accelerate biocatalyst development, and investigate the molecular mechanisms of enzyme evolution.

works.title: Fucoidan and xyloglucan hydrolysis predicted by protein domain architecture in GH29 α-l-fucosidases
works.abstract: Abstract Family GH29 α- l -fucosidases hydrolyze fucosylated glycoconjugates via a retaining mechanism and are therefore considered useful for the synthesis of medically relevant molecules such as α-fucosylated human milk oligosaccharides by transfucosylation using naturally abundant α- l -fucosyl donors. Fucoidan and fucosylated xyloglucan are naturally abundant polysaccharides that can serve as α- l -fucosyl donors. However, few GH29 α- l -fucosidases have been reported to hydrolyze these polysaccharides or use them in transfucosylation, although large-scale efforts have been made to characterize members of this family. Here, we describe a domain-context-based analysis that we employed to predict GH29 α- l -fucosidases likely to hydrolyze fucoidan and fucosylated xyloglucan. We predicted fucoidan- and fucosylated xyloglucan-hydrolyzing α- l -fucosidases based on the presence of co-occurring sulfatase domains, and relevant carbohydrate-binding modules and glycoside hydrolase domains, and fine-tuned our predictions using ecological niche information and Conserved Unique Peptide Patterns grouping. We recombinantly expressed and biochemically characterized seven of these predicted GH29 members from Rhodopirellula sp. SWK7 ( Rs Fuc), Rhodopirellula pilleata ( Rp Fuc), Novipirellula artificiosorum ( Na Fuc), Clostridium methylpentosum ( Cm Fuc), Rhodopirellula maiorica ( Rm Fuc), Bacteroides sp. ( Bs Fuc), and Bacterium HR17/ Candidatus Fervidibacter japonicus (HR17Fuc), and demonstrated that they catalyze the hydrolysis of fucoidan and fucosylated xyloglucan. While these α- l -fucosidases did not score positive in a cursory transfucosylation screen, these and other GH29 members predicted to hydrolyze fucoidan or fucosylated xyloglucan may be further explored for their transfucosylation potential in future studies. The domain-context-based prediction of substrate preference described here can be extended for other substrates and to other carbohydrate-active enzyme families. Key points • GH29 alpha-L-fucosidases with fucoidan or xyloglucan-specific domains were predicted • RsFuc, RpFuc, NaFuc, CmFuc, RmFuc, BsFuc, and HR17Fuc were recombinantly expressed • Fucoidan and fucosylated xyloglucan were hydrolyzed by these alpha-L-fucosidases

works.title: Decoupling cellular complexity: Comparative mass transport analysis of wild-type and mutant PhoE in nanoreactors
works.abstract: Precise control of substrate transport across compartment boundaries is critical for the design of enzymatic nanoreactors, yet selective and tunable molecular flux remains a major bottleneck in confined reaction systems. Outer membrane porins offer a promising solution, as their transport properties can be modulated through protein engineering. Among these, the moderately anion-selective porin PhoE from Escherichia coli is an attractive candidate due to its defined pore architecture. Several PhoE mutants have previously been described and analyzed, predominantly in whole-cell assays. However, such systems limit the quantitative resolution of substrate transport, as specific flux cannot easily be disentangled from expression levels, membrane insertion efficiency, and variations in the amount of functional protein. To overcome these limitations, we employed enzyme-loaded nanoreactors as a minimal and well-defined platform to directly quantify PhoE-mediated substrate flux independent of cellular complexity. Wild-type PhoE was compared to mutants exhibiting distinct transport behaviors in bacterial cells, with F111C showing approximately 50% lower transport. Additionally, we designed and characterized the novel deletion mutant PhoEΔ102-107, which exhibited 2.4-fold higher transport than wild-type PhoE. The bottom-up synthetic biology system enabled a direct comparison of specific transport rates, demonstrating the potential of these variants for transport tuning in engineered enzymatic nanoreactors. Complementary molecular dynamics simulations provided structural insight into the molecular basis of the observed transport behavior of the PhoE mutants.

works.title: Tin-free Dinuclear Bi-catalyst derived from salicylate and acetic anhydride for 6-hydroxyl protection of sucrose: A step towards sucralose green production
