Oxygen-modified C2N-supported Mo4 cluster as a high-performance catalyst for CO2 electroreduction to C1 and C2 products: A DFT study
Magnetic MnFe2O4 catalyst supported on biochar for selective catalytic oxidation of cellulose-derived p-xylene to p-tolualdehyde
Atomically dispersed Ni sites paired with sulfur vacancies in CdS for photocatalytic hydrazine-assisted nitroarene hydrogenation

Tailoring the interfacial architecture of Pd/cellulose-L-arginine-rice hull-hercynite spinels via in situ maleic acid polymerization for efficient molecular oxygen activation: kinetic-thermodynamic insights into chemoselective aerobic ethylbenzene oxyfunctionalization
Engineering a C─N Lyase for Enantioselective Hydroaminations With Secondary Amines
works.abstract: C─N lyases from the aspartase/fumarase superfamily are attractive biocatalysts for the production of noncanonical amino acids via selective hydroamination of α , β ‐unsaturated carboxylic acids. However, the substrate scope of these enzymes remains largely restricted to primary amines, as secondary amines are usually poorly accepted. Here, we report the engineering of ethylenediamine‐ N , N’ ‐disuccinic acid (EDDS) lyase for enantioselective hydroaminations with secondary amines as non‐native substrates. This engineered C─N lyase variant (Y26A/Q159V/R294E) not only displays a 20‐fold increase in activity for dimethylamine addition to fumarate, but also processes secondary amines that show no reactivity with the wild‐type enzyme. Expanding the substrate scope of this C─N lyase to include secondary amines establishes a viable enzymatic platform for the enantioselective synthesis of structurally diverse tertiary amines.

works.title: Electro‐Biocatalytic Dearomative Oxidation–Asymmetric Aldol Cascade Enables Direct Synthesis of Chiral 3‐Hydroxyindolin‐2‐Ones From Indoles
works.abstract: We present a sustainable electro‐biocatalytic cascade for the highly diastereo‐ and enantioselective synthesis of pharmaceutically relevant 3‐hydroxyindolin‐2‐ones by combining electrochemical dearomative oxidation of indole followed by an abiotic CALB‐catalyzed asymmetric aldol reaction in the same reaction vessel. The versatility of the electro‐biocatalytic cascade was well explored with a wide range of substrates, including indole‐bearing electron‐donating, ‐withdrawing, and halide substituents, along with two representative cyclic ketones, which were successfully transformed into the desired products in moderate to excellent yields (up to 91%) with outstanding stereocontrol, providing up to 99% ee and 99% de . Furthermore, mechanistic investigations, including control experiments and cyclic voltammetry studies, revealed distinct roles for electricity and enzyme catalysis and provided evidence for the involvement of iodinated intermediates in dearomative electrochemical oxidation of indole. The synthetic utility of the cascade protocol was further demonstrated through gram‐scale synthesis. This work establishes a versatile electro‐biocatalytic cascade platform that integrates the sustainability of electrosynthesis with the exceptional selectivity of enzyme catalysis, providing a sustainable and efficient process for the stereoselective synthesis of chiral 3‐hydroxyindoline‐2‐ones.

works.title: Modular benzylamine synthesis through trifunctional zirconium catalysis
Pulling sugars off salt activation
Ru/rutile-TiO2 catalysts with coverage-independent particle size and shape enable isolation of particle density effects in polyolefin hydrogenolysis
Tuning Supported Fe-Ag Catalysts for Selective Acetylene Hydrogenation: A Combined Experimental and Computational Study
works.abstract: Abstract The selective hydrogenation of acetylene is a key reaction step for purification in ethylene production, as trace amounts of acetylene can poison downstream polymerization catalysts. Industrial acetylene hydrogenation is currently performed almost exclusively using palladium-based catalysts, motivating the search for more abundant alternatives. In this study, supported Fe-Ag catalysts with different Fe:Ag ratios were synthesized and evaluated for the selective hydrogenation of acetylene under industrially relevant front-end conditions. The catalysts were characterized by XRD, N2-physisorption, TPR, XPS, STEM-EDX, ICP-OES and XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs were used to investigate composition-dependent trends in adsorption energetics. Catalyst characterization revealed no evidence for the formation of an extended Fe-Ag alloy phase after air exposure. Instead, Fe- and Ag-rich domains were found to coexist in close nanoscale proximity providing a structural basis for considering possible local Fe-Ag interactions. Accordingly, the DFT calculations were performed on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs to investigate how the local chemical environment around adsorption sites affects the adsorption energetics of reaction intermediates. DFT calculations predict a gradual weakening of adsorption strength with increasing local Ag content, while the experimental catalyst series independently shows a decrease in ethane selectivity with increasing Ag loading. Under CO-containing front-end conditions, catalyst selectivity increased further due to competitive adsorption effects, while the influence of catalyst composition became less pronounced. The combined experimental and computational results indicate that changes in the local Fe-Ag environment influence adsorption energetics and may contribute to the composition-dependent catalytic behavior in acetylene hydrogenation. These findings provide design principles for the development of palladium-free hydrogenation catalysts based on earth-abundant metals.

works.title: Catalytic Stereoselective Inverse Electron Demand Formal Aza-Diels–Alder: Access to Highly Congested Molecular Bowl-Shaped 3D Tertiary Amines
works.abstract: Abstract Diastereoselective sp3-rich heteroatom-based bowl-shaped polycyclic molecules are a key structural scaffold in various bioactive molecules. Due to the inherent steric congestion of these structures, achieving precise stereochemical control remains a significant challenge in contemporary synthetic chemistry. We herein disclose a practical iron-catalyzed assembly of an indole-derived tertiary amine-based pentacyclic molecule through an intermolecular, iminium-triggered dearomative inverse electron-demand formal aza-Diels–Alder (IEDFADA) reaction. Detailed computational and deuterium labelling experiments strongly suggest that the diastereoselective formation of this complex core involves a stepwise in situ generation of a short-lived, highly reactive azadiene. Moreover, the negative slope (ρ = –0.29) from the Hammett plot indicates the formation of a partial positive charge and that the electron-donating groups enhance the reaction rate. Notably, the concise tagging of drug molecules and downstream synthetic transformations with good yields and diastereoselectivity should highlight the potential applications of this methodology in drug discovery settings in medicinal chemistry.

works.title: Interpretable Machine Learning Accelerated Discovery of Doped Spinel Co3O4 Catalysts for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
works.abstract: Abstract The discovery of doped spinel Co3O4 electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hindered by the large catalyst design space and the high computational cost of density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Here, we establish a hierarchical interpretable machine learning (ML) framework that decouples electronic structure prediction from catalytic activity prediction. By starting with predicting the electronic descriptor (d-band center) from readily accessible structural descriptors and subsequently predicting adsorption energetics, the framework removes the need for expensive electronic structure DFT calculations during catalyst screening while preserving physical interpretability. A random forest model was trained on adsorption free energies of OH*, O*, and OOH* from 144 representative active sites and achieved a test mean absolute error of 0.21 eV. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified surface energy, active site undercoordination, and the d-band center as the dominant descriptors governing adsorption energetics. To avoid additional DFT calculations of the d-band center during screening, a second ML model predicted it directly from structural and elemental descriptors with a test mean absolute error of 0.23 eV. The resulting framework enabled rapid evaluation of OER overpotentials across 252 active sites, while subsequent targeted DFT calculations identified Al-, Ca-, Fe-, and Mn-doped Co3O4 as promising candidates. Targeted DFT calculations and electrochemical measurements further validated the improved OER activity of Al- and Fe-doped Co3O4. This work establishes an interpretable and computationally efficient strategy for connecting structural descriptors, electronic properties, adsorption energetics, and experimentally measurable catalytic activity, thereby accelerating the discovery of high-performance spinel oxide catalysts.

works.title: Accelerating CO2 Biocatalysis through Multimodal AI-Guided Enzyme Prioritization and Spatial Confinement
works.abstract: Abstract Direct biological conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals is severely restricted by sluggish enzyme kinetics and inefficient intracellular carbon flux. Here, we address these catalytic bottlenecks by synergizing multimodal deep learning, mechanistic enzyme engineering, and synthetic organelle assembly. Using CASKP, a TransKP-guided candidate-prioritization framework that integrates sequence representations with a docking-derived scalar feature, we prioritized and experimentally identified a highly active β-carbonic anhydrase, PbCA, for improving intracellular CO2 supply. Structural analysis and molecular dynamics simulations guided the design of the R71A and V112A variants. The R71A–V112A variant displayed a specific activity of 26.1 U/mg and increased the intracellular 13C-labeled 3-phosphoglycerate ratio 4.9-fold. The simulations were consistent with a more hydrated active-site environment and a strengthened Tyr108-centered hydrogen-bond network. To overcome diffusion and thermodynamic limitations, these optimized biocatalysts were encapsulated into hybrid carboxysomes and coupled with an ATP-generating carboxykinase. 13C tracing confirmed incorporation of inorganic carbon into l-malate, with 95.2% of malate detected as 13C-labeled isotopologues. Subsequent promoter optimization yielded an l-malate titer of 22.7 g/L. This multiscale approach provides an integrated strategy for heterotrophic CO2-incorporating biocatalysis.

works.title: Structural Insights and Functional Expansion of an Aerobic Skatole Synthase
works.abstract: Abstract SktA from the cyanobacterium Nostoc punctiforme NIES-2108 belongs to the versatile heme oxygenase-like domain-containing nonheme oxidase superfamily, whose natural function is to transform 5-bromotryptophan (5-Br-Trp) to 5-bromoskatole in an oxygen-dependent manner. As SktA is also capable of transforming tryptophan (Trp) to skatole, this enzyme represents a skatole synthase that operates under aerobic conditions. Here, the crystal structure of SktA and its complex with 5-Br-Trp and Trp are reported. The amino acids responsible for the substrate binding and the diiron cluster formation were revealed, and their roles in the catalytic reaction were examined via mutagenesis experiments. In addition, we found that SktA is capable of transforming 7-bromotryptophan and 5,7-dibromotryptophan to yield 7-bromoskatole and 5,7-dibromoskatole, respectively, and resolved the crystal structures of SktA in complex with these alternative substrates to elucidate the plasticity of the substrate-binding pocket. Finally, we show that combining SktA and regiospecific self-sufficient Trp halogenases in one-pot reaction systems efficiently transforms Trp to 5-bromo-7-iodo-skatole or 5-iodo-7-bromo-skatole. In summary, this study reveals the structural information, substrate scope, and potential applications in synthetic biology as a module to generate differentially halogenated skatoles of SktA.

works.title: A bioluminescence immunosensor using engineered antibody for quantitative detection of African swine fever virus
works.abstract: Abstract African swine fever (ASF), caused by ASF virus (ASFV), poses a significant threat to global swine industries due to its high mortality and the lack of an effective vaccine. Consequently, it is critical to develop a rapid and quantitative detection method for timely monitoring of swine populations and accurate confirmation of ASF infection, thereby enhancing ASF prevention and control measures. Here, we developed an ultrasensitive bioluminescence immunosensor for quantitative detection of ASFV p30 (p30-UBI) by genetically fusing HiBiT (an 11-amino-acid peptide that binds the NanoLuc fragment LgBiT with high affinity, reconstituting bright bioluminescence) to the light chain constant region of monoclonal antibody (mAb) 16-5E7E8 as the detection antibody and using mAb 2-1B3G3 as the capture antibody. The p30-UBI exhibited broad linear ranges of 46 pg/mL to 250 ng/mL for recombinant p30 protein (a combined quantitative range covered by two calibration equations) with detection limits of 15.3 pg/mL. The practical utility of the p30-UBI was evaluated using tissue, serum, and swab samples from ASFV-challenged pigs. P30 was readily detectable in tissue and serum samples, whereas lower concentrations were measured in swabs, and p30 levels showed broadly similar patterns to ASFV p72 gene copy numbers determined by quantitative PCR (qPCR). Notably, in an exploratory analysis in which pigs from different vaccine groups and dose groups were combined, lower serum p30 levels at 7 dpc were significantly associated with longer survival after ASFV challenge (Spearman ρ = − 0.62, P < 0.0001, n = 53). These findings indicate that the p30-UBI is a promising quantitative analytical method evaluated in samples from experimentally infected pigs. Key points • A HiBiT-tagged antibody-based bioluminescence immunosensor was developed for ASFV p30 detection • The assay achieves detection limits of 15.3 pg/mL for p30 within 70 min • Lower serum p30 levels at 7 dpc were associated with longer survival in an exploratory analysis

works.title: Titanium-perovskite MTiO3-based S-scheme heterojunctions: Materials design and photocatalysis applications
N‐Heterocyclic Carbene‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Monoacylation of Prochiral Diols to Access Axially Chiral Tetraarylethenes
works.abstract: Tetraarylethene is a valuable structural motif, which is widely used in biological probes and imaging, advanced bio‐ and chemosensing platforms, and multifunctional theranostic agents. Therefore, the development of straightforward and efficient methods for the synthesis of axially chiral tetraarylethenes is of great significance. Herein, we report an NHC‐catalyzed atroposelective desymmetrization strategy that enables efficient access to axially chiral tetraarylethenes. The methodology is distinguished by its reliance on readily available starting materials, mild reaction conditions, high functional‐group tolerance, and excellent stereoselectivity. Furthermore, the approach facilitates late‐stage modification of complex natural products, highlighting its utility for synthetic innovation and drug discovery.

works.title: Electrochemical and Photochemical Transformations of Tertiary Formamides
works.abstract: Compared with primary and secondary formamides, tertiary formamides are particularly difficult to activate due to the absence of N─H protons and increased steric hindrance around the nitrogen center. Traditionally, their transformation has relied heavily on stoichiometric oxidants or strong nucleophilic/electrophilic reagents. Over the past decade, the flourishing development of electrochemistry and photochemistry has provided entirely new paradigms for tertiary formamides transformation. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in electrochemical and photochemical‐promoted transformations of tertiary formamides. Based on the types of key intermediates generated and the roles they play, we classify these reactions into six categories: formation of acyl radicals; formation of aminyl radicals; formation of N ‐alkyl carbon‐centered radicals; formation of N ‐acyliminium ions; acting as nucleophiles; and acting as electrophiles. This framework elucidates the intrinsic connections among different reaction pathways and provides a clear trajectory for understanding the activation modes of tertiary formamides under electrochemical and photochemical conditions.

works.title: Recent Advances in Ni‐Catalyzed Asymmetric Dicarbofunctionalization of Alkenes
works.abstract: The asymmetric dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes via nickel catalysis represents a robust platform for the rapid synthesis of enantioenriched compounds from inexpensive and readily obtainable precursors. This approach enables the one‐step addition of two carbon fragments to an alkene, thus providing rapid access to intricate chiral structures that would be difficult to construct using conventional multistep sequences. The unique redox flexibility of nickel, together with its ability to engage radical intermediates and suppress competitive β‐hydride elimination, has enabled diverse enantioselective transformations under reductive, photoredox, and directing‐group‐assisted manifolds. Recent advances have delivered a broad range of asymmetric carboarylation, carboalkenylation, carboacylation, carboalkylation, carbocyanation, and cyclization‐type dicarbofunctionalization reactions. These developments not only expand the synthetic utility of nickel catalysis but also provide valuable opportunities for stereocontrolled C─C bond formation. Recent progress in the nickel‐catalyzed asymmetric dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes, focusing on reaction design, substrate generality, stereochemical control, and mechanistic insights. Current challenges and future opportunities are also discussed, including broader substrate generality, greener reductive systems, electrochemical variants, and more predictive models for enantioselective nickel catalysis.

works.title: Ru‐Doped ZrO 2 as Efficient Electrocatalyst for Hydrogen Evolution Reaction in Acid Electrolyte
works.abstract: The development of efficient and durable electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is crucial for proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE). While zirconium oxide (ZrO 2 ) is chemically stable in sulfuric acid, its poor intrinsic conductivity and sluggish reaction kinetics limit its practical application. Herein, we report a series of ruthenium‐doped zirconium oxide (ZrO 2 /Ru‐x) catalysts synthesized via a facile one‐step hydrothermal method and systematically investigate the effect of ruthenium (Ru) doping content on their HER performance in 0.5 M H 2 SO 4 . The characterization results confirm that Ru atoms are successfully incorporated into the ZrO 2 lattice. Electrochemical measurements reveal that the HER activity exhibits an inverted volcano‐shaped dependence on Ru doping level, while the electrochemical capacitance surface area (ECSA) values display a volcano‐shaped dependence on Ru doping level. Among the prepared catalysts, the optimal ZrO 2 /Ru‐0.75 composition demonstrates the most outstanding performance, with a low overpotential of only 302 mV to achieve 10 mA cm −2 and a small Tafel slope of 119 mV dec −1 , significantly outperforming pristine ZrO 2 and other doped counterparts. This enhanced activity is attributed to the synergistic effect of optimized Ru‐O‐Zr coordination, which promotes water dissociation and facilitates favorable hydrogen adsorption/desorption energetics, as further supported by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). Moreover, the optimized catalyst exhibits excellent long‐term stability over 24 h of continuous electrolysis, underscoring its potential as a cost‐effective alternative to noble‐metal–based HER catalysts. This work provides a comprehensive understanding of the structure‐activity relationship in Ru‐doped ZrO 2 systems and offers a viable strategy for designing high‐performance acidic HER electrocatalysts.

works.title: Structure‐Guided Design of a Selective Fluorogenic Probe for Monitoring Butyrylcholinesterase Activity in Living Cells
works.abstract: Butyrylcholinesterase (BuChE) is an important modulator of cholinergic signaling whose activity increases in several pathological contexts, including neurodegeneration and metabolic dysfunction. However, selective chemical tools for monitoring BuChE activity in complex biological systems remain limited, largely due to its high structural similarity to acetylcholinesterase (AChE) and the deeply buried nature of its catalytic site. Here, we report a series of activatable fluorescent probes based on a 1,8-naphthalimide scaffold for selective BuChE sensing. Probe performance was systematically optimized by varying ester substituents (cyclopropyl, cyclobutyl, cyclopentyl, and cyclohexyl) at the recognition site and by incorporating self-immolative linkers to spatially decouple the fluorophore from the enzymatic trigger. Among the probes developed, the cyclopropyl ester derivative JCB-3 exhibited superior performance, displaying high selectivity for BuChE over acetylcholinesterase (AChE), a low detection limit of 0.84 U/L, and a rapid fluorescence turn-on response within 20 min. Molecular docking studies supported the favorable binding of JCB-3 within the BuChE catalytic pocket. In live-cell imaging experiments, JCB-3 demonstrated excellent cell permeability, low cytotoxicity, and robust activation by endogenous BuChE. Together, these findings establish JCB-3 as a selective chemical probe for imaging BuChE activity and provide mechanistic insight into steric factors that govern cholinesterase selectivity.

Unseen but Avoidable: How Impurities Bias Electrocatalysis from Interface to Interpretation
works.abstract: Abstract Impurities exert profound effects on electrocatalytic measurements and interpretations. Trace levels of contaminants introduced through electrolytes, electrodes, gases, or cell materials routinely generate false activity signals, accelerate degradation, and alter product selectivity. This review categorizes impurity effects by functional impact, including misleading activity, compromised stability, and shifted selectivity, and offers strategies to recognize, isolate, and mitigate these influences. We argue that reliable and reproducible electrocatalytic data require an impurity-aware approach, integrating both experimental protocols and systems engineering. By intentional design, impurities can be transformed from hidden liabilities into controlled variables, ensuring that reported advances in electrocatalysis reflect intrinsic catalyst properties and translate into durable energy technologies.

works.title: Surface-Engineered BiVO4 Photocatalyst Enables Selective Water Oxidation for Water Splitting via a Photocatalysis–Electrolysis Hybrid System
works.abstract: Abstract Selective water oxidation in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions remains a major challenge for photocatalytic systems. BiVO4 is one of the most efficient visible-light-responsive photocatalysts for water oxidation and exhibits high activity in Fe3+-mediated water-oxidation systems. However, although accumulated Fe2+ can introduce competing oxidation pathways under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ redox conditions, effective strategies for suppressing these processes and maintaining selective water oxidation remain largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a surface-engineering strategy that overcomes this limitation in BiVO4. Systematic investigation revealed that the poor activity of BiVO4 under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions arises not only from catalyst degradation but also from competition with Fe2+ oxidation reactions. Surface modification of BiVO4 with W species, originally intended to improve acid durability, not only suppressed catalyst dissolution but also mitigated Fe2+-related performance losses, resulting in a marked enhancement of photocatalytic water oxidation. The activity enhancement correlated with highly dispersed surface W species localized near the outermost region of BiVO4. Notably, the highest activity was obtained before or near the onset of detectable WO3 crystallization, suggesting that the surface state of W species in this temperature range is more closely associated with the enhanced activity than crystalline WO3 domains under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ conditions. The optimized photocatalyst maintained efficient water oxidation while suppressing Fe2+-related performance losses, achieving an apparent quantum yield of 63% under Fe3+-based conditions and approximately 30% even under strongly acidic and concentrated Fe(ClO4)3 conditions relevant to hybrid water splitting. The optimized photocatalyst maintained selective water oxidation even as Fe2+ accumulated to approximately 100 mM, enabling nearly quantitative Fe3+-to-Fe2+ conversion under strongly acidic conditions. When incorporated into a photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid system, the enhanced photocatalytic activity was directly translated into approximately 1.5-fold higher water-splitting performance than that of the benchmark H-Fe-Cs-WO3 system. These findings demonstrate that selective water oxidation can be maintained even in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions through appropriate photocatalyst surface engineering, providing a useful strategy for photocatalysts operating in redox-mediated reaction environments, including photocatalysis–electrolysis hybrid water-splitting systems.

works.title: Bacillus subtilis as a heterologous host for production and secretion of a hyperthermostable archaeal subtilisin-like protease
works.abstract: Abstract Pernisine is a subtilisin-like protease from the hyperthermophilic archaeon Aeropyrum pernix . Its ability to degrade resistant protein substrates such as prion proteins makes this protease attractive for industrial applications. Here, we used Bacillus subtilis as a heterologous host for expression and secretion prepropernisine, a precursor of pernisine. The native secretion signal peptide of prepropernisine was replaced with a signal peptide of native B. subtilis preprosubtilisin E to achieve efficient secretion. Among the four promoters tested, xylose-inducible promoter yielded the highest level of propernisine production, with a titer of 175 mg per l of culture. The produced propernisine was purified from the culture medium using a combination of ultrafiltration, anion-exchange chromatography, and heat treatment. Approximately 115 mg of propernisine with 80% purity was obtained per liter of culture, representing a 10-fold higher yield than previously achieved with other heterologous hosts. Activated pernisine obtained from B. subtilis exhibited remarkably high thermostability, with optimal activity at temperatures above 90 °C and across a pH range of 7 to 9. In addition, it retained approximately 60% of initial activity after autoclaving and efficiently degraded collagen and meat. The stability and performance of pernisine from B. subtilis were nearly identical to that of pernisine produced in Escherichia coli . Overall, these findings demonstrate that B. subtilis is a promising host for further optimization of cultivation conditions and scale-up to controlled bioreactor cultivation, to achieve production of pernisine at industrial level. Key points • Bacillus subtilis efficiently produced and secreted recombinant propernisine. • Propernisine was readily purified from the culture medium. • Activated pernisine exhibited high thermostability and efficient meat hydrolysis.

From Promiscuity to Specificity: Machine Learning-Driven Multidimensional Evolution of Tropinone Reductase for Challenging Substrates
works.abstract: Abstract A fundamental challenge in harnessing substrate promiscuity for industrial biocatalysis lies in reconciling broad substrate acceptance with high catalytic specificity. Although promiscuous enzymes provide attractive starting points for accessing non-natural transformations, their native active-site architectures and conformational dynamics often lack the precision required for efficient and selective conversion of desired unnatural substrates. Thus, systematically decoding and reprogramming the interplay between promiscuity and specificity remains a key obstacle toward versatile biocatalysts. Here, we address this challenge by integrating virtual screening, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulations into a unified engineering framework. A tropinone reductase from Cochlearia officinalis (CoTR) was identified as a broadly promiscuous scaffold. By converting complex enzyme–substrate interaction dynamics into quantifiable and actionable design principles, we predict and validate key residues that govern substrate promiscuity. Guided by these insights, distinct CoTR variants were engineered for three representative substrates. The optimized variants—CoTR‑8M, CoTR‑5M‑1, and CoTR‑5M‑2—exhibited 7.0‑ to 16.3‑fold higher catalytic efficiencies than wild-type CoTR toward their respective target substrates and supported substrate loadings of up to 50 or 100 g L–1 while maintaining >99% ee. This work not only delivers scalable routes to three industrially valuable chiral alcohols but also provides mechanistic insights into the synergistic modulation of promiscuity and specificity. This study demonstrates a general strategy for translating intricate molecular-recognition features into rational design principles, thereby facilitating the development of tailored biocatalysts for non-native substrates.

works.title: L-Threonine production from acetate by metabolically engineered Corynebacterium glutamicum using a pH-controlled fed-batch process
works.abstract: Acetate has a considerable potential as a non-food feedstock for microbial bioproduction, yet its use for amino acid production remains underexplored. Here, we developed a process for L-threonine production from acetate as the sole carbon source with Corynebacterium glutamicum by integrating rational, genome-based metabolic engineering with pH-coupled fed-batch cultivation. The engineered strain AT-3 carried five chromosomal mutations that alleviated feedback inhibition of key enzymes and redirected carbon flux toward the aspartate pathway. Substrate supply was controlled using a custom Visual Basic-based feeding script that automatically adjusted the acetic acid feed in response to online pH measurements. Robust process performance was maintained during a tenfold scale-up from 100-mL DASbox to 1-L DASGIP bioreactors. The optimized process achieved an L-threonine titer of 10.04 g/L and a yield of 0.086 g/g acetate. This study provides a basis for further studies on the development and improvement of acetate-based amino acid production process. KEY POINTS: • Plasmid-free C. glutamicum strains produce L-threonine in acetate minimal medium • pH-controlled acetic acid feed in bioreactors improved L-threonine production • Acetate-based production of feed amino acids avoids competition with human food.
