Ball‐Milling‐Enabled Pd‐Catalyzed One‐Pot Cross‐Coupling of Aryl Thianthrenium Salts With In Situ Generated Reformatsky Enolates
works.abstract: Mechanochemistry enables an efficient Pd‐catalyzed cross‐coupling of aryl thianthrenium salts with in situ generated Reformatsky‐type enolates. Ball milling plays a dual role by promoting both the activation of zinc to form Reformatsky‐type organozinc enolates from α ‐halo esters and amides and their subsequent cross‐coupling with solid aryl thianthrenium salts. This single‐step one‐pot protocol provides access to a broad range of α ‐arylated products in high yields within short reaction times. The mechanochemical process is performed under ambient conditions without requiring an inert atmosphere, highlighting its operational simplicity and practicality. Furthermore, the methodology is readily applicable to the late‐stage functionalization of structurally complex bioactive molecules.

works.title: Photoelectrochemically Driven Hydrophosphorylation of Alkynes to Access ( E )‐Alkenylphosphine Oxides
works.abstract: The current metal‐free methods for the hydrophosphorylation of alkynes, encompassing both electrochemical‐driven and photoredox‐catalyzed processes separately, show efficacy only when applied to less hindered terminal alkynes, polarized internal alkynes, or aryl alkyl internal alkynes; diaryl acetylenes are found to be incompatible with these conditions. Both methods involve a radical stepwise addition, yielding a Z / E isomeric mixture with the Z ‐alkenylphosphine oxides as the primary products. Furthermore, electrochemical hydrophosphorylation of alkynes is prone to double reduction of alkynes during extended reaction times. Herein, in sharp contrast to conventional, often separate, electrochemical or photoredox catalytic approaches that typically produce a Z / E isomeric mixture, this photoelectrocatalytic (PEC) process, which combines photocatalysis and electrochemistry, exclusively furnishes stereospecific ( E )‐alkenylphosphine oxides as the sole products. Significantly, this protocol successfully applies efficiently to diaryl acetylenes and bulky terminal alkynes, with no iterative addition of triple bonds observed.

works.title: Para ‐Selective C─H Amination of Benzenepropanamides via Photocatalytic N ‐Centered Radical‐Mediated Dearomatization
works.abstract: We report a photocatalytic strategy for constructing para ‐aminobenzenepropanamide scaffolds. This method employs oxime‐ester‐based diamination reagents as dual‐radical precursors to generate imino and amidyl radicals. The key step involves N ‐centered radical‐mediated intramolecular dearomatization, forming the cyclohexadienyl radical (CHDR) intermediate. This protocol features mild reaction conditions and broad functional group tolerance. Furthermore, this method achieves selectivity that is not affected by the stereochemical or electronic properties of the benzene ring, thereby enabling the efficient synthesis of 4‐aminobenzoylamide.

works.title: Interfacial Co–Ni Dual‐Site Synergy in Confined Co 9 S 8 –Ni 3 S 2 Heterostructures for Electrocatalytic Water Splitting
works.abstract: Although heazlewoodite‐type nickel sulfide (Ni 3 S 2 ) exhibits promising hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity, its application in overall water splitting remains limited by sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics associated with insufficient water activation. Herein, Co 9 S 8 –Ni 3 S 2 heterostructures confined in nitrogen‐rich spongy carbons are constructed to regulate interfacial electronic properties and unlock Co–Ni catalytic synergy for efficient water electrolysis. A melamine sponge is employed as a 3D scaffold to direct the spatial anchoring of Co 2+ and Ni 2+ precursors, followed by in situ sulfidation and carbonization to form a conductive porous carbon framework with confined sulfide heterointerfaces. The resulting heterointerfaces trigger significant spin polarization and electron redistribution from Ni 3 S 2 to Co 9 S 8 through interfacial Co–S–Ni configurations, thus activating the Co–Ni dual sites for enhanced water adsorption and dissociation. The catalyst exhibits outstanding bifunctional OER/HER activity and long‐term stability in alkaline media, while an alkaline electrolyzer assembled with the catalyst requires only 1.515 V to deliver 10 mA cm −2 . Moreover, in situ and ex situ analyses reveal dynamic reconstruction of the Co–Ni sites under OER conditions, continuously generating additional active centers and sustaining high catalytic activity. This work paves a new way for designing earth‐abundant and high‐performance heterostructured electrocatalysts toward green hydrogen production.

works.title: Multicomponent Reactions Enabled by Photoinduced Formal Alkyl Transfer of Tertiary Amines
works.abstract: Multicomponent reactions (MCRs) provide a powerful and efficient strategy for rapidly accessing structurally diverse compounds under mild conditions. Among MCRs, the Ugi‐type reactions—including the Ugi–azide variant—hold a central role in the synthesis of α‐amino derivatives. Historically, research in this area has largely focused on expanding the scope of nucleophiles to access novel and complex products. However, most reported transformations still rely on imine (or iminium) intermediates generated from primary/secondary amines and aldehydes/ketones. In this work, we disclose a photochemical approach that utilizes photoexcited aromatic amines to trigger the oxidation of tertiary amines, leading to the formation of iminium species. These intermediates undergo a formal alkyl transfer process with aromatic amines to generate new iminium salts, which subsequently engage with various nucleophiles in a multicomponent fashion. This strategy enables the efficient synthesis of three important classes of functional molecules—α‐amino phosphine oxides, tetrazoles, and imides—via a tertiary amine‐involved MCR under light irradiation.

works.title: Influence of Supports on Electrocatalytic Performance of Dual‐Atom Catalysts
works.abstract: Due to excellent atomic usage, stability, activity, and selectivity, dual‐atom catalysts (DACs) have attracted a lot of attention in electrocatalysis. The dispersion, electrical structure, stability, and catalytic reaction dynamics of the functional sites are all directly influenced by the chemical and physical properties of the supports, including specific surface area, pore structure, conductivity, and surface chemical state. Here, the support categorization and structure design of DACs are examined. To expedite the development of high‐performance DACs and uncover the structure–performance relationship, a sensible modulation technique is subsequently put out. Furthermore, the dynamic evolution of diatomic sites during the electrocatalytic processes is demonstrated using sophisticated characterization techniques. Afterward, the applications of DACs in energy conversion devices and electrocatalysis are examined. Finally, the potential and problems associated with the continued development of DACs for energy‐related applications are presented.

works.title: Boosting Co‐Catalyzed [2+2+2]‐Cyclotrimerizations Through Strong π‐Acceptor Ligands
works.abstract: α‐Cationic phosphine ligands are strong π‐acceptors that significantly enhance the electrophilicity of transition‐metal centers. Herein, we demonstrate their effectiveness in cobalt‐catalyzed [2+2+2] cyclotrimerization of alkynes, enabling the efficient synthesis of trisubstituted benzenes under mild conditions. The use of these ligands leads to a marked increase in catalytic activity, allowing reactions to proceed at room temperature and with catalyst loadings as low as 2 mol%. Results obtained with two different α‐cationic phosphines, cyclopropenio‐ and pyridiniophosphine, suggest that enhanced π‐backdonation to the α‐cationic phosphine increases the electrophilicity of the cobalt center, thereby promoting cyclization. The methodology displays broad substrate scope and high regioselectivity, including challenging sterically hindered alkynes. These results highlight the potential of α‐cationic phosphines to boost the performance of earth‐abundant metal catalysts and advance sustainable catalytic strategies.

works.title: Application of Bifunctional Togni’s Reagent in Photoredox‐Catalyzed Oxytrifluoromethylation of Alkenes
works.abstract: We report a radical‐based protocol for the photoredox‐catalyzed oxytrifluoromethylation of alkenes with Togni’s reagent. This strategy provides efficient access to a broad array of CF 3 ‐containing esters and is also applicable to late‐stage functionalization of drug molecules under mild conditions. Moreover, conversion of the resulting CF 3 ‐functionalized esters to other valuable building blocks is also achieved. Mechanistic investigations reveal that Togni’s reagent acts as both a trifluoromethyl and an acyloxy group. Consequently, the difunctionalization reaction can proceed without any external nucleophiles, offering high atom economy.

works.title: Transition‐Metal‐Free Mechanochemical Construction of C─P Bonds Using Diazonium Salts With H‐Phosphonates and Phosphine Oxides
works.abstract: A transition‐metal‐free mechanochemical protocol for the construction of C─P bonds is reported. The reaction employs aryldiazonium tetrafluoroborates and bench‐stable P(O)─H compounds (H‐phosphonates and phosphine oxides) under solvent‐free ball‐milling conditions at room temperature. In contrast to a previously reported radical‐based mechanochemical C─P coupling utilizing stoichiometric magnesium and phosphoryl chlorides, our method operates via an ionic nucleophilic substitution pathway, as supported by the lack of inhibition by TEMPO and 1,1‐diphenylethylene and the accelerating effect of electron‐donating substituents. The protocol displays a broad substrate scope (43 examples, up to 96% yield), excellent functional group tolerance, and gram‐scale applicability, providing a practical and sustainable route to arylphosphonates and arylphosphine oxides.

works.title: Photoinduced Synthesis of ( Z )‐ β ‐Sulfonamido Enamines via an Electron Donor–Acceptor Complex With N ‐(Sulfon)amido Pyridinium Salts
works.abstract: A novel, visible‐light‐driven, transition‐metal, and photocatalyst‐free methodology for the C(sp 2 )–H amination of enamines has been developed, enabling the regio‐ and stereoselective synthesis of ( Z )‐ β ‐sulfonamido enamines from readily accessible N ‐aminopyridinium salts. This new protocol provides straightforward access to a broad range of ( Z )‐ β ‐sulfonamido enamines (32 examples, 31%–78% yields) and proceeds via an electron donor–acceptor complex‐initiated radical pathway, as supported by mechanistic studies. Its synthetic robustness was further demonstrated through a gram‐scale reaction, one‐pot three‐component processes, and successful application to natural sunlight‐driven transformations. The utility of this method in pharmaceutical chemistry was highlighted by the late‐stage functionalization of amino‐containing drug derivatives. Overall, this operationally simple and mild strategy offers an efficient new platform for constructing functionalized enamine derivatives of synthetic significance.

works.title: Advances in the Phosphorus Functionalization Reactions of Stable Enamines
works.abstract: Enamines are well known for their highly versatile and distinctive reactivity toward the generation of molecular diversity and complexity. By reacting with phosphorus‐based reagents, enamines are able to generate a broad array of phosphorus containing organic products, providing practical accesses to structurally diverse phosphorus‐functionalized small molecules through different reaction pathways. Herein, based on our longstanding interest and the recent advances in this area, the advances in the phosphorus functionalization of stable enamines are reviewed. According to the feature of the key transformations, the reactions based on the vinyl C–H functionalization, π‐bond functionalization, the cascade cyclization reaction, and other related reactions are introduced and discussed individually.

works.title: Characterization and Molecular Engineering of a Thermostable Amino Acid Dehydrogenase for Enhanced ( S )‐2‐Amino‐1‐Butanol Synthesis
works.abstract: ( S )‐2‐Amino‐1‐butanol, a key intermediate for ethambutol hydrochloride synthesis, is currently produced via heavy metal‐catalyzed processes or enzymatic resolution with limited theoretical yields. While amine dehydrogenases (AmDHs) offer sustainable alternatives for asymmetric reductive amination, their applicability is often restricted by narrow substrate scope. Here, we report the discovery of a thermostable amino acid dehydrogenase from Thermoactinomyces daqus ( Td AADH) that exhibits optimal activity at pH 9.0 and 55 °C with exceptional thermostability ( t 1/2 = 21 days at 40 °C). Although inactive toward the non‐native substrate 1‐hydroxy‐2‐butanone, structure‐guided engineering via site‐directed and iterative saturation mutagenesis (ISM) successfully endowed the enzyme with desired functionality: the initial double mutant K93S/N288L (M1) acquired de novo amination activity, while subsequent evolution to the quintuple mutant M4 (incorporating L136T/T139D/M141R) enhanced specific activity by 2.75‐fold (5.38 U·g −1 ) without compromising enantioselectivity ( ee > 99%). Mechanistic investigations via molecular docking suggest that these mutations plausibly reshape the substrate‐binding pocket, alleviate steric hindrance, and optimize electrostatic interactions to accommodate the hydroxyketone substrate. Preparative‐scale biotransformation (40 °C, 30 mM substrate, coupled with GDH/glucose for cofactor recycling) achieved quantitative conversion (≥99%) within 36 h. This work expands the enzymatic toolbox for thermostable AmDHs.

works.title: The Dual Nature of RNA Ligation and Degradation by T4 RNA Ligase 1: Insights Into an AMP‐Driven, Nucleobase‐Dependent Reverse Reaction
works.abstract: T4 RNA Ligase 1 (Rnl1) catalyzes the ligation of a 5'-phosphate to a 3'-hydroxyl in single-stranded RNA and is widely used in RNA biotechnology for applications such as RNA library preparation and 3'-adapter ligation. In addition to ligation reaction, Rnl1 catalyzes the reverse reaction, leading to RNA degradation. However, how RNA sequence affects susceptibility to this reverse reaction remains unclear, and practical strategies for controlling it through buffer conditions have not been established. Previous studies showed that AMP promotes and ATP suppresses the reverse reaction; we confirmed these effects by electrophoretic analysis of FAM-labeled RNA homopolymers, a substrate not previously examined. Furthermore, using miRNA substrates, we demonstrated that the reverse reaction can occur under conditions that more closely resemble the practical conditions in which Rnl1 is used, thereby extending the relevance of previous findings. Additionally, we showed that the Rnl1-mediated reverse reaction exhibits pronounced nucleobase preference. The reverse reaction is suppressed by elevated temperature and duplex formation. Furthermore, experimental results combined with stochastic simulations indicate that Rnl1-mediated degradation proceeds via an endonucleolytic mechanism. These findings define how reaction conditions and nucleobase difference influence reverse reaction efficiency and provide practical guidance for minimizing RNA degradation while maintaining ligation efficiency.

works.title: Development of Highly Efficient Lysosome‐Targeting Peptide Ligands for the Internalization of Extracellular Proteins
works.abstract: Lysosome-targeting chimeras (LYTACs) induce the internalization of extracellular and membrane-associated proteins by routing them to lysosomes via endogenous receptors, such as the insulin-like growth factor-2 receptor (IGF2R), also known as cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor. While current IGF2R ligands are effective, expanding the LYTAC toolkit with structurally simple and synthetically accessible ligands remains a practical necessity. Here, we first validated that previously reported dimeric and monomeric peptides induce robust internalization, establishing them as effective IGF2R-targeting LYTAC ligands. To further optimize the peptide architecture, we performed systematic mutational scanning on its monomeric sequence to simplify the peptide architecture. We identified the L4 variant, which features a single leucine substitution at the fourth position. This optimized monomer induces greater internalization efficiency than the previously reported wild-type monomeric peptide ligand. To demonstrate its utility, we conjugated the L4 recruiter to a specific PCSK9 binder. The resulting bifunctional molecule successfully induced the dose- and time-dependent internalization of PCSK9. Collectively, these findings establish several peptide variants as practical and highly effective building blocks for the development of extracellular protein internalization platforms.

works.title: Explorations of the Hydrogenation of D 2 by Nitrogenase
works.abstract: A non‐physiological substrate of the enzyme nitrogenase, D 2 , is doubly hydrogenated by the enzyme to produce 2HD. This ‘HD reaction’ is in competition with the native function of the enzyme, hydrogenating N 2 to NH 3 . At the active site of the enzyme, a gallery of H atom donors is identified, and the proposed complete cycle mechanism for the N 2 reaction uses these donors eight times to generate the 2NH 3 + H 2 products. Here, the functionality of these H atom donors in hydrogenating D 2 to 2HD is investigated, applying density functional simulations to a 480+ atom model of the active site including all important surrounds. Many possible reaction trajectories were explored, and a revised mechanism for the HD reaction is presented. The mechanisms for hydrogenation of D 2 and of N 2 have common components, accounting for their experimentally known competition. Consideration of ten items of relevant experimental data about the HD reaction shows how the proposed mechanism complies with and interprets these data, although two experimental observations are still to be checked.

Iridium-catalysed para-C–H activation and borylation of native aromatic carboxylic acids
Duplex qPCR for detection and discrimination of wild-type and persistent O foot-and-mouth disease virus
works.abstract: Abstract Foot-and-mouth disease (FMD), predominantly caused by serotype O foot-and-mouth disease virus (FMDV), remains highly contagious and economically devastating worldwide. A significant challenge in disease control is that recovered or vaccinated animals can become asymptomatic carriers of persistent strains (Op), which are indistinguishable from acute wild-type (WT) strains using current diagnostic methods. In this study, we developed a duplex TaqMan real-time PCR assay based on comparative next-generation sequencing and genomic analysis of WT and persistent O FMDV strains. Conserved regions were identified for universal detection, and Op-specific single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) mutations were targeted for differential amplification using ARMS-PCR (amplification refractory mutation system PCR). The optimized assay, consisting of a co-detection channel and a typing channel, demonstrated excellent specificity with no cross-reactivity against host nucleic acids or unrelated cell lines, a detection limit of 5 copies/µL, and clear differentiation of WT from Op strains. Furthermore, the duplex assay successfully distinguished wild-type and persistent strains in infected cell samples and across different viral passages (PI30 and PI60). This duplex TaqMan RT-qPCR assay provides, for the first time, a sensitive, specific, and efficient tool for simultaneous detection and differentiation of wild-type and persistent O FMDV strains in infected cell samples and across viral passages. Although clinical validation remains to be performed, this assay offers a promising basis for further studies on FMD surveillance and the detection of viral persistence. Key points • First duplex TaqMan RT-qPCR assay differentiating wild-type and persistent O FMDV. • Detection limit of 5 copies/µL with no cross-reactivity against host nucleic acids. • Differentiates Op strains at passages 30 and 60, monitors persistence, aids control.

works.title: Culture of Chlorococcum sp. NITD25 in diluted whey water: Organic load removal and biomass characterization
Physico-chemical and bioactive properties of spray-dried microparticles from Neltuma ruscifolia leaf extract
Distinction between Listeria species and L. monocytogenes serotypes with a handheld, VNIR hyperspectral imaging camera
works.abstract: Abstract A handheld, visible near-infrared (VNIR) hyperspectral imaging (HSI) camera was used to differentiate between Listeria species ( L. monocytogenes , L. ivanovii and L. innocua ) and two L. monocytogenes serotypes: 1/2a and 4b. The results indicated that portable HSI cameras could effectively be used for pathogen detection and distinction applications, despite lower spectral resolution and higher sensitivity to noise when compared to benchtop CCD-based instruments. Five hundred and fifty-five hyperspectral images were collected from pure cultures on agar plates throughout seven sampling campaigns. Sixty-five percent of samples/isolates ( n =± 90 samples per class) were used to train Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) models and 35% of samples ( n =± 50 samples per class) were used for validation. An overall classification accuracy (validation) of 74.5% was achieved for species-level discrimination through a four-class model ( L. monocytogenes 1/2a, L. monocytogenes 4b, L. ivanovii and L. innocua ), which demonstrates moderate performance within the VNIR range. However, Species-level performance was uneven across classes, with lower validation accuracies for L. innocua (68.0%) and L. ivanovii (63.0%) compared to L. monocytogenes 1/2a (71.8%) and 4b (95.2%). In contrast, a two-class model achieved ~ 90% accuracy for serotype-level discrimination between L. monocytogenes serotypes 1/2a and 4b. This highlights a novel use of portable VNIR cameras as a rapid, non-destructive serotyping aid. Variable Importance in Projection (VIP) score plots were used to characterise valuable wavelengths in the visible range that were significant for discriminant analysis, for example, 690 nm was significant for the classification of L. innocua , whilst 871 nm was associated with L. ivanovii. Notably, all the significant absorption regions used to differentiate between the L. monocytogenes serotypes were in the visible range (480–525 nm, 540–560 nm, 610 nm and 690 nm) despite the colony morphology being virtually identical for these organisms on brain heart infusion agar. Key points • A portable HSI camera was used to distinguish between Listeria colonies on agar • PLS-DA accuracy of 74.5% was obtained for classification between Listeria species • PLS-DA accuracy of 90% obtained for classification between L. monocytogenes serotypes

works.title: Dimyristoylphosphatidylcholine vesicle treatment enhances the storage stability and culturability of Lactococcus lactis suspensions
works.abstract: Abstract Maintaining bacterial culturability during storage is important for microbial biotechnology. This study evaluated dimyristoylphosphatidylcholine (DMPC) liposomes as a treatment for Lactococcus lactis suspensions stored for 28 days at 4 °C and room temperature. Liposomes were formed by thin-film hydration in the presence of bacterial cells. Cryogenic scanning electron microscopy (cryo-SEM) revealed approximately 100–160 nm vesicular structures in the DMPC-only sample and similar nanostructures near cells in treated suspensions, without establishing a continuous coating. On day 28 at 4 °C, treated and untreated suspensions had apparent zeta potentials of −17.31 and −1.56 mV, respectively. Across storage conditions and sampling times, polydispersity indices were 0.34–0.42 for treated suspensions versus 0.46–0.87 for controls, indicating lower apparent size heterogeneity. At room temperature on day 1, turbidity, expressed as optical density at 600 nm, was 0.99 versus 0.43, respectively. Metabolic activity assessed by 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)− 2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) reduction reached 2.50 versus 0.93 MTT-reducing units under the same conditions and subsequently declined, reaching 0.35 units in treated suspensions on day 14. Culturability was higher in treated suspensions from day 7 onward at both temperatures. On day 28 at room temperature, treated and untreated samples contained 2.55 × 10 5 and 3.83 × 10 1 CFU · mL −1 , respectively. DMPC liposome treatment thus supported retention of culturability during storage, with a larger relative benefit at room temperature, although the underlying vesicle-cell interactions remain unresolved. Key points • DMPC liposome treatment was associated with lower PDI in L. lactis suspensions. • DMPC treatment preserved L. lactis culturability during prolonged storage. • The protective effect of DMPC was strongest during room-temperature storage.

works.title: Integrative Multi-Cohort Analysis of hsa-miR-1277, hsa-miR-301b, and hsa-miR-519a-1 Reveals Diagnostic Potential and Regulatory Associations in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
works.abstract: BACKGROUND: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a highly heterogeneous malignancy characterized by extensive molecular dysregulation, including aberrant microRNA (miRNA) expression. Identification of clinically relevant miRNAs and their associated regulatory networks may improve understanding of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) biology and facilitate biomarker discovery. OBJECTIVE: The present study aimed to identify novel dysregulated miRNAs associated with OSCC and to investigate their potential diagnostic relevance, predicted target interactions, and functional pathway associations through integrative transcriptomic and clinical validation analyses. METHODS: Mature miRNA expression profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-HNSCC cohort were retrieved through the UCSC Xena Browser and analyzed using DESeq2 following anatomical site-based filtering to obtain HPV-negative OSCC samples. Differentially expressed miRNAs were identified using adjusted p-value < 0.05 and |log2FoldChange|≥ 0.5 thresholds. Based on differential expression patterns and limited prior characterization in OSCC, hsa-miR-1277, hsa-miR-301b, and hsa-miR-519a-1 were selected for downstream analyses. Kaplan-Meier survival, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), integrative target prediction, Pearson correlation, STRING protein-protein interaction network, Gene Ontology (GO), and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses were subsequently performed. Independent validation was carried out using four Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) cohorts and qRT-PCR analysis in Indian OSCC clinical specimens. RESULTS: Differential expression analysis identified 283 significantly expressed miRNAs in OSCC, including 167 upregulated and 116 downregulated transcripts. ROC analysis demonstrated strong discriminatory performance for hsa-miR-301b (Area Under the Curve = 0.868) and moderate performance for hsa-miR-1277 (AUC = 0.735), whereas hsa-miR-519a-1 exhibited comparatively limited diagnostic utility. Integrative target prediction identified five high-confidence targets each for hsa-miR-1277 and hsa-miR-301b, while hsa-miR-519a-1 demonstrated a broader overlap profile comprising 24 candidate genes. Functional enrichment analyses demonstrated enrichment of neuronal signaling, synaptic regulation, ion channel activity, neuroactive ligand-receptor interaction, and cadherin-associated pathways among candidate target genes. Validation across independent GEO cohorts and clinical specimens demonstrated heterogeneous expression patterns with partial concordance to TCGA-derived observations. CONCLUSION: This integrative multi-cohort analysis identifies hsa-miR-1277, hsa-miR-301b, and hsa-miR-519a-1 as novel miRNA candidates associated with OSCC-related molecular dysregulation. The findings further highlight the substantial biological heterogeneity underlying HNSCC and emphasize the challenges associated with translating large-scale transcriptomic signatures into reproducible clinical biomarkers.

Vitamin B 12 ‐Functionalized Nanogels for pH‐, and Redox‐Responsive Doxorubicin Delivery
works.abstract: Rapidly proliferating cancer cells display an elevated demand for vitamin B 12 , rendering this bacterial‐derived cofactor an attractive targeting motif for nanotherapeutic drug delivery. Herein, we report a concise two‐step synthesis of a polymerizable 5′‐modified vitamin B 12 ‐monomer that enables the covalent integration of B 12 into pH‐ and redox‐responsive nanogels. The resulting nanogels efficiently encapsulate doxorubicin through electrostatic interactions between the cationic drug and the anionic nanogel network, while enabling stimuli‐responsive drug release under tumor‐relevant conditions. In vitro studies revealed that DOX@B 12 ‐nanogels retain potent antiproliferative activity against HT‐29 colorectal cancer cells (IC 50 = 0.878 ± 0.102 μM), while decreasing cytotoxicity toward healthy CCD 841 CoN cells by 34‐fold relative to non‐B 12 ‐functionalized control nanogels. These findings establish covalently engineered vitamin B 12 ‐nanogels as a promising platform for selective and stimuli‐responsive anticancer drug delivery.

works.title: From off-target to on-demand: Precision engineering and translational evaluation of next-generation base editors
Auto-aggregation characteristics and EPS interface-driven mechanisms of a novel salt-tolerant nitrate-reducing bacterium Thauera sp. Z-1
Chloroidium sp. and Tetradesmus obliquus biomass for plant biostimulants: Extraction, characterization and bioactivity on seeds development
works.abstract: ABSTRACT Microalgal biomass has emerged as a promising feedstock for producing sustainable plant biostimulants (PBs), particularly when cultivating microalgae using residual nutrients and CO 2 sources. This study focuses on the extraction of PBs from Chloroidium sp. and Tetradesmus obliquus microalgae cultivated in anaerobic digestion liquid digestate and their impact on seeds development. Alcalase enzymes-assisted extraction at 50 °C emerged as the most efficient method, achieving protein extraction yields of 47.78 ± 1.94% (equivalent to 16.0 ± 0.6% of the biomass dry weight) for Chloroidium sp., and 16.24 ± 1.13% (equivalent to 8.1 ± 0.6% of the biomass dry weigh) for T. obliquus . The influence of protein or peptide size on the potential of the PBs was evaluated using three fractions of the extracts: < 3 kDa, 3-100 kDa, and >100 kDa. Optimized extracts were evaluated on mustard and wheat seeds, revealing a dose-dependent relationship between the potential of the PBs and their molecular sizes. Interestingly, the biostimulant activity of T. obliquus extracts on mustard was attributed to the medium-sized fraction. In contrast, Chloroidium sp. extracts required a synergistic interaction between different molecular sizes to enhance root growth across both seed species. This study reveals species-dependent biological activity of microalgae-based PBs.

works.title: Violet Phosphorus Nanodots for Long‐Term Cell Imaging With Persistent Intracellular Stability
works.abstract: Long‐term cellular imaging probes with high photoluminescence intensity/stability and high biocompatibility are crucial for advanced in vitro cell imaging and long‐term cell tracing. However, conventional organic fluorescent dyes are prone to photobleaching and require assistance to enter cells. Here, NH 2 ‐PEG‐NH 2 was adopted to modify violet phosphorus quantum dots to obtain PEG‐VPNDs with strong and stable photoluminescence, where bond contacts were built between NH 2 ‐PEG‐NH 2 and phosphorus through P─N and P─O to keep robust structures. The PEG‐VPNDs have been demonstrated to have outstanding photoluminescence stability both in solution and intracellular environments. No photoluminescence decay was observed after 60 days of storage under ambient conditions or after continuous irradiation with a 300 W xenon lamp for 3 h, in contrast to the photobleaching observed in organic fluorescent dyes. The PEG‐VPNDs were also demonstrated to easily enter A2780 and SKOV3 cells and stay outside the nucleus without any assistance, where no decay was observed for photoluminescence of PEG‐VPNDs even for 96 h. The PEG‐VPNDs have been demonstrated to have high viability in A2780 and SKOV3 cells with concentration of 144 ppm. The photoluminescence performance with high intracellular stability and high biocompatibility makes PEG‐VPNDs a promising candidate for long‐term bioimaging, cell tracing and other biomedical applications.

Support-induced reaction pathway switching in Cu-catalyzed deoxygenation of biomass-derived palmitic acid

Nitrogen ion beam mutagenesis improves sophorolipid production and properties in Starmerella bombicola
works.abstract: Abstract Sophorolipids (SLs) are microbial biosurfactants with broad industrial potential, but their large-scale application relies on robust high-producing strains with desirable functional properties. In this study, Starmerella bombicola CGMCC 1576 was subjected to nitrogen (N+) ion beam mutagenesis to improve SL production and product performance. A mutant library containing 124 isolates was constructed, and two stable high-producing mutants, 2–21 and 3–5, were obtained through high-throughput screening and shake-flask validation. Mutant 2–21 preferentially accumulated acidic sophorolipids (ASL) and showed the highest total sophorolipid (TSL) production, whereas mutant 3–5 produced more lactonic sophorolipids (LSL). HPLC profiling showed that the mutants retained the major SL components of the parental strain but differed markedly in component abundance and product distribution. Transcriptional analysis revealed upregulation of genes associated with fatty acid utilization, SL biosynthesis and metabolite transport, particularly in mutant 2–21 at 96 h, suggesting enhanced precursor conversion and product accumulation. Functional assays further showed composition-dependent differences in surface activity and mildness. LSL-rich fractions exhibited stronger surface activity, while ASL-rich fractions showed lower zein solubilization and hemolytic activity. In 100-L bioreactor fermentation, mutant 2–21 produced 224.31 g/L TSL, confirming its scalability and production robustness. These results demonstrate that N+ ion beam mutagenesis is an effective strategy for developing high-producing S. bombicola strains and tailoring SL composition for functional applications. Key points Nitrogen ion beam mutagenesis improved SL production in S. bombicola.ASL-rich and LSL-rich mutants showed distinct SL profiles.Mutant 2–21 produced 224.31 g/L TSL in a 100-L bioreactor.

works.title: Identification and functional characterization of RepE variants that increase plasmid copy number
works.abstract: Abstract Replication of low-copy-number iteron plasmids is tightly controlled by initiator proteins that coordinate replication initiation with transcriptional autoregulation. In the F-plasmid system, RepE fulfills both functions through a balance between monomeric and dimeric forms. Here, random mutagenesis of the repE gene combined with high-stringency selection was used to identify variants that modulate plasmid copy number. Two point mutations, A78S and Q45L, were identified and shown by qPCR and ddPCR to increase the copy number of plasmid pFO1 relative to the parental repE(R118P) allele. The mutations exhibited growth-phase-dependent effects, with A78S having a stronger impact during exponential growth and Q45L during stationary phase. A double mutant showed a cumulative effect, particularly in exponential phase. RepE transcription increased in the presence of pFO1 and correlated with plasmid copy number, supporting a titration-based regulatory model. These findings demonstrate that engineering RepE variants enables tunable control of plasmid copy number, offering a useful strategy for optimizing gene dosage in synthetic biology and biotechnological applications. Key points • RepE variants enable fi ne-tuning of plasmid copy number. • Gene dosage can be modulated without changing plasmid architecture. • RepE engineering off ers potential applications in biotechnology.

works.title: Dual-origin probiotic formulation attenuates intestinal inflammation in experimental colitis
works.abstract: Abstract Intestinal inflammation associated with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is driven by complex interactions between host immunity and gut microbiota, necessitating alternative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional immunosuppressive drugs. In the present study, a dual-origin probiotic formulation comprising Lactobacillus plantarum AG40V (plant-derived) and Lactobacillus fermentum HO17HF (human-derived) was developed and evaluated for its safety and anti-inflammatory efficacy in a 2,4,6-trinitrobenzenesulfonic acid (TNBS)-induced colitis model in Sprague–Dawley rats. The formulation (1012 CFU/mL; 1:1 ratio) exhibited stability under refrigerated conditions and demonstrated significant in vitro functional antioxidant activities. Acute and sub-acute oral toxicity studies, conducted in accordance with OECD guidelines, confirmed the safety of the formulation, with no mortality or significant alterations in physiological, haematological, biochemical, or histopathological parameters. In the TNBS-induced colitis model, oral administration of the probiotic formulation resulted in marked attenuation of intestinal inflammation, as evidenced by reduced levels of nitric oxide, myeloperoxidase, and lipid peroxidation, along with enhanced catalase activity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the dual-origin probiotic formulation is safe and functionally effective in mitigating intestinal inflammation through modulation of oxidative stress and host inflammatory responses. This study highlights the translational potential of ecologically diverse probiotic consortia as a promising strategy for the management of inflammatory gastrointestinal disorders. Key points Dual-origin probiotics showed safety in experimental colitisTreatment reduced inflammation and improved gut healthFindings support probiotic potential in inflammatory bowel disease

works.title: Expanding the structural landscape of cytochrome P450 reductases and the effect of redox mediators on CYP-catalyzed reactions
works.abstract: Abstract Cytochrome P450 reductases (CPRs) are microsomal diflavin oxidoreductases that transfer electrons from nicotinamide cofactors to class II cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs). CPRs can also reduce other proteins, including cytochrome b 5 , heme oxygenase, and components of the fatty acid elongation system, as well as nonphysiological acceptors such as cytochrome c , ferricyanide, and various drugs. Although structural and functional studies have provided valuable insights into CPRs, the available data remain insufficient to fully elucidate their electron transfer mechanism and interactions with diverse redox partners. Here, we report the structural and functional characterization of two fungal CPRs from Candida albicans ( Cal CPR) and Mycosarcoma maydis (formerly Ustilago maydis , Uma CPR) and compare their properties with previously characterized CPRs. N -terminal truncation enabled soluble expression in Escherichia coli , and kinetic parameters were determined using cytochrome c and ferricyanide. Although Uma CPR shares greater sequence similarity with ascomycete CPRs than with mammalian CPRs, its overall structure displays features more closely resembling mammalian CPRs, including its FAD-binding topology. We further investigated the ability of both CPRs to support C. albicans CYP52A21 activity and evaluated the effects of reaction environment and redox mediators on CYP–CPR reconstitution. Both truncated CPRs supported CYP activity, with CPR performance strongly influenced by the reaction environment. Addition of the redox mediator cytochrome b 5 from M. maydis significantly enhanced product formation, including when a nonnative CPR was used. These findings highlight the structural diversity and functional plasticity of CPRs and demonstrate that the broader redox environment can strongly influence CYP–CPR efficiency, extending the complexity of electron transfer beyond the canonical CYP–CPR pairing. Key points • CPRs from ascomycetes and basidiomycetes fungi exhibit distinct structural features. • The CPR from Mycosarcoma (Ustilago) maydis is structurally more similar to mammalian CPRs. • CYP-CPR activity is strongly influenced by reaction environment and cytochrome b5 and extends beyond the canonical protein pairing.

works.title: Valorization of Macadamia and Bambara agro-wastes into poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) by Bacillus cereus DUT-Y04: optimization and functional characterization
works.abstract: Polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) are biodegradable and biocompatible polymers that have emerged as sustainable alternatives to petroleum-based plastics. Despite their potential, large-scale commercialization remains limited by high production costs, largely driven by the use of expensive carbon substrates. This study investigated the valorization of Macadamia nut shells (MNS) and Bambara groundnut shells (BGS) as renewable feedstocks for bacterial PHA production. Among the screened isolates, Bacillus cereus DUT-Y04 was identified as a potent PHA producer. Key fermentation variables influencing PHA accumulation were identified using the Plackett–Burman Design (PBD) and subsequently optimized through Response Surface Methodology (RSM). Under optimal conditions, PHA accumulation reached 54.96% of the cell dry weight, yielding 3.10 g/L, representing a 5.85-fold increase over the unoptimized titer (0.53 ± 0.01 g/L). The process achieved a biomass yield ( Y x/s ) of 0.48 g/g and a PHA titer ( Y p/s ) of 0.26 g/g, with 62.10% substrate utilization efficiency and a good overall growth rate ( μ = 0.08 h -1 ). FTIR and GC–MS analyses indicated that the recovered polymer was predominantly poly(3-hydroxybutyrate) (P(3HB)). Thermal analysis revealed a heat-flow transition in the 155–180°C region and a maximum degradation rate at 225°C, confirming thermal characteristics comparable to commercial-grade P(3HB). This study demonstrates the potential of underutilized agricultural residue hydrolysates as a sustainable carbon source for microbial PHA biosynthesis.
