Mild Generation of Vinyl, Methyl, Heteroaryl, and Cyclopropyl Radicals From Boronic Esters via Photoinduced Deboronation
works.abstract: The photoinduced deboronative generation of unstabilized radicals, including vinyl, methyl, heteroaryl, and cyclopropyl radicals, from commercially available and easy‐to‐handle boronic esters under mild conditions in a two‐molecule photoredox system was achieved. The generated unstabilized radicals readily added to electron‐deficient alkenes, resulting in new C─C bond formation without transition metals.

works.title: Ultrafast MAS and Deuteration for High‐Resolution Proton Detected Solid‐State NMR of Intact Fungal Cell Walls
works.abstract: Glycans are the main components of the fungal cell wall and play a central role in fungal pathogenesis, making atomic‐level structural and dynamic insight into these biopolymers essential for the development of new antifungal therapeutics. 1 H‐detected solid‐state NMR (ssNMR) at fast magic‐angle spinning (MAS) offers an unprecedented opportunity to study glycan site, specifically at atomic resolution in intact fungal cell walls. However, the 1 H resolution and sensitivity in ssNMR are often limited for detailed studies, especially for rigid and highly heterogeneous samples, such as intact fungal cells. Here, we conducted a detailed study on 1 H line width and 1 H T ′ 2 coherence times in the rigid core of the human pathogenic Candida albicans fungal glycans at 60–150 kHz MAS rates and partial fungal cell wall deuteration schemes. We showcased the possibilities and limitations of 1 H‐detected multidimensional 1 H/ 13 C chemical shift assignment experiments for rigid cell wall glycans. Furthermore, we probed dynamics using relaxation measurements, providing access to motions spanning from nanoseconds to microseconds. Overall, we demonstrated significant methodological advances in 1 H‐detected ssNMR spectroscopy, achieving unprecedented 1 H resolution of rigid glycans in intact fungal cell walls. These developments could be applicable for ssNMR detailed studies of intact cell walls in other human pathogens.

works.title: Cytoplasmic Lipid Membrane Biogenesis in Prokaryotes: From Soluble Lipid Building Blocks to a Dynamic and Functional Boundary Layer
works.abstract: Prokaryotic membranes are fundamental to cellular organization and function, serving as dynamic platforms for transport, energy conservation, signaling, environmental adaptation, etc. This review provides an overview of prokaryotic membrane architecture, highlighting the structural diversity of bacterial and archaeal cell envelopes, focusing on the cytoplasmic membranes and the distinct lipid chemistries that define them. By describing the general pathways for fatty acid and phospholipid biosynthesis, we emphasize the universal role for the lipid intermediates lysophosphatidic acid and phosphatidic acid, as well as the major lipid species phosphatidylethanolamine, phosphatidylglycerol, and cardiolipin of the diderm bacteria Escherichia coli. Besides synthesis, lipid membrane insertion is described, highlighting recent findings regarding lipid leaflet distribution, asymmetry, and intermembrane transport. Altogether, these processes provide a general overview of lipid composition and function of proliferating cells.

works.title: From Dysbiosis to Disease: How Vaginal Microbiota Shape Group B Streptococcus Pathogenesis
works.abstract: Host-microbe interactions refer to the dynamic relationships between hosts, such as humans, and the microorganisms present on or inside them. These associations can be beneficial, like gut bacteria facilitating digestion, or harmful, such as pathogens leading to disease. This review focuses on the reproductive tract, specifically the vaginal microbiome. Typically, a healthy vaginal microbiome is dominated by Lactobacillus species, which help protect against infections by pathogens. Dysbiosis, or a microbial imbalance, allows pathogens to invade. One such pathogen is Streptococcus agalactiae (group B Streptococcus, GBS), which can colonize the vaginal microbiome and cause infections. GBS infection during pregnancy is particularly concerning and is a major cause of adverse pregnancy outcomes. This review will explore host-microbe interactions in the vaginal microbiome, with an emphasis on GBS infection, its virulence, and current treatment strategies.

works.title: Water regulates interface access and reactivity in CO2 electrolysis
Inducing local heating fields in ferromagnetic high-entropy alloys to inhibit (bi)carbonate formation for durable CO2 electroreduction
Phytochemical profiling, antioxidant activity, and antibacterial activity of fruit extracts from three Melastoma species against aquatic pathogens
Latex proteases from Cryptostegia grandiflora as an alternative coagulant for cheesemaking
works.abstract: Latex proteases from Cryptostegia grandiflora were used to induce milk-clotting and then, for cheesemaking using traditional artisanal procedures. The cheese was submitted to texture and sensory analysis. The proteolytic fraction (Cg-coagulant) exhibited optimal milk coagulation at 3 mg/mL and induced rapid curd formation (11 min), faster than commercial chymosin (35–45 min). The resulting cheese (Cg-cheese, 47% moisture) showed a slightly higher yield (13.03 % w/w/ yield) compared with cheese produced using a commercial rennet (11.91 % w/w/ yield). Proximate composition analyses of Cg-cheese curd revealed moisture, protein, and fat contents comparable to those of cheeses produced with Calf rennet. Cg-cheese presented higher titratable acidity (0.63 % LA) and higher pH (7.67; 6.86 for cheese curd) than the control cheese. Heavy metal content was well below regulatory limits and microbiological analyses indicated absence of Salmonella , Escherichia coli , and coagulase-positive Staphylococcus , per gram of cheese sample. Texture profile of Cg-cheese revealed significantly lower hardness, cohesiveness, and gumminess compared with cheeses produced with commercial rennet, resulting in a grainy structure similar to ricotta rather than that of commercial cheese curd. Sensory evaluation revealed high consumer acceptance, with acceptability exceeding 70% for all attributes and above 85% for color and appearance. Furthermore, 67% of participants expressed purchasing intention. Cg-coagulant was not cytotoxic to fibroblasts at 62.5 μg/mL. It induced slightly dermatitis in 12 % of subjects and did not produce noticeable adverse effects in participants of the sensory analysis. These results suggest that Cg-coagulant represent an alternative to Calf-rennet for cheesemaking grainy.

works.title: Behavioral and metabolic profiling of endogenous lipids conversion to carotenoids in Rhodosporidium toruloides under sugar depletion
Redox‐Neutral C(sp 3 )─H Alkenylation via Photocatalyzed Tandem Hydrogen Atom Transfer and Downstream Oxidative Radical Polar Crossover
works.abstract: Herein, we present a photocatalytic route that exploits a redox‐neutral tandem hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and oxidative radical polar crossover (RPC) manifold. This method enables the efficient synthesis of valuable allylic amides and ethers through the valorization of three classes of ubiquitous feedstock chemicals: carboxylic acids as precursors to hydrogen atom abstractors, amides or ethers as C(sp 3 )─H donors, and olefins as radical acceptors. The protocol operates under mild conditions, exhibits broad functional group tolerance, and is readily scalable. The redox‐neutral nature of this transformation mechanistically distinguishes it from traditional net‐oxidative approaches associated with exogenous stoichiometric oxidants. Crucially, it allows HAT substrates bearing “hydridic” C─H bonds (e.g., α ‐ to heteroatom: X─C H R 1 R 2 ) to be engaged in Giese‐type addition reactions and subsequent oxidative RPC/nucleophilic trapping, where traditional net‐oxidative approaches inevitably result in Shono‐type further oxidation of the HAT‐derived radical (e.g ., α ‐ to heteroatom: X + ═CR 1 R 2 ) and nucleophilic interception prior to intermolecular radical addition.

works.title: Iodanyl Radical Catalysis Enables Ring‐Opening and δ‐C─H Functionalization of Aliphatic Alcohols
works.abstract: Iodanyl radical catalysis offers distinct reactivity beyond conventional two‐electron hypervalent iodine manifolds. However, existing catalytic protocols rely predominantly on complex bis‐iodoarene platforms to stabilize radical intermediates, whereas simple monodentate aryl iodides remain poorly developed due to off‐cycle pathways. Herein, we report that 2‐iodopyridine serves as a highly efficient organo‐iodine catalyst for photocatalytic iodanyl radical catalysis under mild, redox‐neutral, and metal‐free conditions. Integrated within a visible‐light photoredox cycle, this protocol achieves direct single‐electron activation of unfunctionalized aliphatic alcohols to generate reactive alkoxy radical intermediates. This dual catalytic manifold facilitates both ring‐opening functionalization of cyclic alcohols via β‐scission and site‐selective δ‐C─H functionalization of linear alcohols through 1,5‐hydrogen atom transfer. Mechanistic investigations and radical trapping experiments support the proposed one‐electron catalytic pathway. This strategy provides an accessible and low‐cost platform for iodanyl radical catalysis, expanding the synthetic utility of native aliphatic alcohols.

works.title: Cloning and characterization of a novel β-glucosidase from Bifidobacterium breve 689b and its application in the preparation of rare ginsenoside F2
works.abstract: The rare ginsenoside F2, exhibiting a wide spectrum of pharmacological activities, is present in the human body and is readily absorbed. However, the extremely low content of ginseng has hindered its development and application. In this study, a glycoside hydrolase gene (BbGlu1B) encoding a Bifidobacterium breve 689b was cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli BL21. BbGlu1B was purified, exhibiting a molecular weight of 44.6 kDa, with optimal activity at 40 °C and pH 6. The purified BbGlu1B exhibited β-glucosidase activity and was able to highly selectively hydrolyse the outer Glu residue at the C-3 position of ginsenoside Rd, yielding the rare ginsenoside F2. The optimal reaction conditions for the preparation of ginsenoside F2 were determined through a one-factor experiment: at 35 °C, pH 6.5, a substrate concentration of 6 mg/mL, and an enzyme addition of 0.29 U/mg, the conversion rate reached over 90%. The structure was characterized using TLC, HPLC,13C-NMR, MALDI-TOF-MS, FTIR, and UV spectroscopy. Molecular docking results revealed that hydrogen bonds formed by key amino acid residues ARG-35, GLY-280, and THR-260 with ginsenoside Rd play a dominant role in mediating the interaction between Rd and BbGlu1B, which is of crucial importance for maintaining the binding stability of Rd and enhancing its catalytic efficiency. In this study, a novel β-glucosidase BbGlu1B possessing exceptional biotransformation activity towards ginsenosides Rd was explored, and a feasible and efficient method for the enzymatic preparation of rare ginsenoside F2 was developed.

works.title: Integrated dual-pathway valorization of Feijoa sellowiana: Adsorption of safranin O and methylene blue and antioxidant capacity evaluation
Photoredox‐Catalyzed Strain‐Release Annulation of N ‐Cyclopropylamides With Diazenes
works.abstract: Pyrazolidines are valuable saturated N–N heterocycles, yet convergent routes from independently variable C3 and N2 components remain limited, particularly when mono‐donor cyclopropanes are employed as C3 synthons. Herein, we report a visible‐light photoredox‐catalyzed strain‐release annulation of mono‐donor N ‐cyclopropylamides with diazenes. The transformation integrates single‐electron‐transfer oxidation of N ‐cyclopropylamides with strain‐driven cleavage of an otherwise electronically unbiased C─C σ bond and dual C─N bond formation, providing direct access to 3‐amidopyrazolidines bearing a cyclic N ‐acyl aminal motif. A broad range of aryl, heteroaryl, aliphatic, and drug‐derived N ‐cyclopropylamides, together with azodicarboxylates, diaryl diazenes, azodicarboxamides, and a cyclic azo reagent, are compatible under mild, metal‐free conditions. Preliminary reactions with N‐ sulfinylamines and an N ‐cyclobutylamide furnish five‐ and six‐membered N,S ‐heterocycles, suggesting that this photoredox platform may be applicable to other heteroatom–heteroatom π components.

works.title: Cu‐ERI Zeolite Catalysts With Tailored Properties for the Removal of N‐Containing Compounds
works.abstract: A series of ERI‐type zeolite materials of different properties was prepared, which led to the obtaining of Cu‐containing ERI materials of distinct catalytic properties in the selective catalytic reduction of NO x with ammonia (NH 3 ‐SCR‐DeNO x ) and the selective catalytic oxidation of ammonia (NH 3 ‐SCO). Various characterization techniques were employed to describe the copper species in the synthesized ERI zeolite in order to understand its NH 3 ‐SCR‐DeNO x and NH 3 ‐SCO activity as well as N 2 selectivity. Cu‐ERI_1 and Cu‐ERI_2 possess the highest amount of active sites (i.e., Cu 2+ species) and thus enhanced activity in the low‐temperature range of NH 3 ‐SCR‐DeNO x (with NO conversion of 83%–93% and N 2 selectivity of 93%–95% at 250 °C). Especially, Cu‐ERI_2 possesses easily reducible Cu 2+ species that are responsible for activation and oxidation of NH 3 . Indeed, steady‐state isotopic transient kinetic analysis of NH 3 ‐SCO revealed the shortest average surface lifetime and the lowest surface concentration of NH 3 over the Cu‐ERI_2 sample. Further, modulation excitation experiments confirmed that NO preferentially consumes NH 3 adsorbed on the Brønsted acid sites on this sample. For other samples, the experiments of NO absorption followed by NH 3 + O 2 exposure and around (NH 3 adsorption and NO + O 2 exposure) indicated that NH 3 adsorbed on Lewis acid sites is preferentially consumed during the reaction process.

works.title: Selective Catalytic Oxidation of Glycerol to 1,3‐Dihydroxyacetone Over Supported Au/CuO–SnO 2 Catalysts: The Influence of Support Preparation Methods
works.abstract: This study investigates how interactions within catalysts impact performance in catalytic oxidation systems. In this work, a series of Cu‐doped SnO 2 supports with different morphologies are synthesized via sacrificial template, hydrothermal, solvothermal, and coprecipitation methods, respectively. And then Au nanoparticles were supported onto the above four supportsthrough urea deposition to obtain Au/CS‐HT, Au/CS‐NS, Au/CS‐YS, and Au/CS‐DP catalysts. Under mild conditions, the Au/CS‐HT catalystexhibited optimal catalytic performance for the conversion of glycerol to 1,3‐dihydroxyacetone (DHA). Glycerol conversion and DHA selectivity reached 62.2% and 81.2%, respectively. Characterization revealed that the sacrificial‐template catalyst’s strong component interactions yield unique crystalline properties: uniformly distributed Cu 2+ ions and abundant oxygen vacancies in SnO 2 enhance oxygen activation, while Au‐support electronic synergistic effect and appropriate basic sites selectively oxidize secondary hydroxyl groups in glycerol. These findings provide new design principles for optimizing metal–support interactions through synthesis methods of support.

works.title: Photochemical Efficient Radical Normalized Transformation of N ‐nitrosamines Triggered by Energy Transfer Process
works.abstract: N ‑nitrosamines are potent carcinogenic contaminants widely present in food, pharmaceutical products, and environmental matrices, posing considerable risks to human health. The accurate detection of these compounds calls for the urgent development of an efficient and chemoselective transformation capable of converting diverse N ‑nitrosamines into a single, stable product. Herein, we report a photochemical radical normalization strategy that achieves this goal via an energy‑transfer process. This methodology enables the synthesis of structurally diverse perfluoroalkyl oximes from N ‑nitrosamines, alkenes, and perfluoroalkyl iodides with up to 99% yields. The protocol exhibits broad functional‑group tolerance, rendering it particularly attractive for the late‑stage functionalization of complex molecules. Mechanistic studies reveal that energy transfer from photoexcited N ‑nitrosamines to perfluoroalkyl iodides concurrently suppresses undesired amino radical formation and promotes perfluoroalkyl radical generation, ensuring high reaction selectivity. Furthermore, this strategy proves applicable to the analysis of various N ‑nitrosamine impurities. Validation experiments using irbesartan active pharmaceutical ingredient batches confirmed the robust quantification of total N ‑nitrosamine content, demonstrating its practical utility in pharmaceutical quality control.

works.title: Visible‐Light‐Promoted Radical Tetrafluoroethylation/Cyclization of N ‐Alkenyl Indoles: Access to Tetrafluoroethylated Pyrrolo[1,2‐ a ]indoles
works.abstract: Tetrafluoroethylated motifs are increasingly widespread in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and functional materials. However, efficient and sustainable methods for their incorporation into complex polycyclic frameworks remain underdeveloped. Herein, we report a visible‐light‐promoted radical cascade cyclization of N ‐alkenyl indoles using readily available 1,2‐dibromotetrafluoroethane (BrCF 2 CF 2 Br) as a tetrafluoroethyl radical source. This mild protocol enables a facile one‐step construction of tetrafluoroethylated pyrrolo[1,2‐ a ]indoles bearing a quaternary carbon center. The reaction exhibits broad functional group tolerance, delivering the desired products in up to 95% isolated yield. Mechanistic studies support a photoredox radical cascade pathway. This work offers a sustainable and operationally simple approach to pharmaceutically relevant fluorinated polycyclic indoles from easily accessible starting materials.

works.title: Radical Strategies to Activate Organoboron Reagents for Cross‐Coupling Reactions
works.abstract: In organic synthesis, organoboron reagents—especially alkylboronic acids and their pinacol esters (APEs)—have attracted significant attention due to their advantages, including low toxicity, ease of handling, and bench stability. Therefore, they are considered attractive alternatives as radical sources. However, it is quite challenging to generate these carbon radicals directly from boron compounds because of their high oxidation potentials and low Lewis acidity. This minireview focuses on recent advances in this area, in which heteroatom radicals are applied to activate boron compounds to generate carbon radicals. The review is organized according to activation mechanisms: bromine radical‐mediated activation, oxygen radical‐mediated processes, nitrogen radical (aminyl radical) transfer strategies, direct photoexcitation of synthesized borate complexes, and other approaches, including triplet–triplet energy transfer, electron donor–acceptor complex formation, and catechol‐mediated thermal initiation. For each of these approaches, we discuss the underlying mechanism, substrate scope, synthetic utility, current limitations, and future development.

works.title: Front Cover: Mild Generation of Vinyl, Methyl, Heteroaryl, and Cyclopropyl Radicals From Boronic Esters via Photoinduced Deboronation (Adv. Synth. Catal. 21/2026)
works.abstract: Photoinduced Deboronation The photoinduced deboronative generation of unstabilized radicals, including vinyl, methyl, heteroaryl, and cyclopropyl radicals, from commercially available and easy-to-handle boronic esters under mild conditions in a two-molecule photoredox system was achieved. The generated unstabilized radicals readily added to electron-deficient alkenes, resulting in new C−C bond formation without transition metals. More in the Research Article (10.1002/adsc.70769), Yasuharu Yoshimi and co-workers.

works.title: Characterization and Crystal Structure Elucidation of the l ‐Homoserine O ‐Succinyltransferase MetXS From Cupriavidus necator H16
works.abstract: Among the promising microbial platforms to produce value‐added products from CO 2 , chemolithoautotrophic bacteria, such as Cupriavidus necator H16 ( C. necator ), stand out due to their ability to fix CO 2 via the Calvin–Benson–Bassham (CBB) cycle. Although C. necator has been extensively studied as a biotechnological production host, several of its biosynthetic pathways remain incompletely characterized at the biochemical level. This includes l ‐methionine biosynthesis, for which genome‐based functional annotations of key enzymes have not been validated experimentally. In this study, we identified and characterized Cn MetXS, a homoserine O ‐succinyltransferase involved in l ‐methionine biosynthesis in C. necator . Biochemical characterization demonstrated that Cn MetXS catalyzes the transsuccinylation of l ‐homoserine to O ‐succinyl‐ l ‐homoserine but exhibits no transacetylase activity. Additionally, we determined the apo crystal structure of Cn MetXS at 1.86 Å resolution, revealing a homodimer with a MetX‐G2 active‐site architecture and distinct conformations of the active‐site lid region. Structural analysis and docking suggest that Arg335 stabilizes the succinylated enzyme intermediate and explains the observed succinyl‐CoA specificity. Together, these results establish the function of Cn MetXS and pave the way for metabolic engineering strategies to produce l ‐methionine in C. necator .

works.title: Investigation of the DSF/Cu Reaction Using HR LCMS and Reactivity Studies
works.abstract: Cuprotosis is a unique mode of cell death being explored in many new therapeutic anticancer studies. A widely used approach is the combination of Cu(II) salts with diethyldithiocarbamate disulfide, disulfiram (DSF), also known as the alcohol‐sensitizing drug Antabuse, which generates the toxic Cu(II)bis(diethyldithiocarbamate), Cu(DTC) 2 , in a complex redox reaction. The mechanism for the generation of Cu(DTC) 2 in this reaction, which we term the DSF/Cu reaction, has been examined using high‐resolution liquid chromatography‐mass spectroscopy (HR LCMS) by monitoring the reaction at different sampling times to determine sequential speciation of reaction intermediates. Other intermediates of this reaction are characterized by the addition of adduct‐forming “traps” used to characterize thiol and sulfenic acid species generated throughout the reaction. The time‐resolved spectra reveal that one initial reaction is a 2‐electron oxidation of a thione moiety in DSF to a sulfine (DSF‐O), which implies a concurrent reduction of Cu(II) to Cu(0). Other results suggest the involvement of Cu(I) in the titled reaction, most likely formed by comproportionation of Cu(0) with Cu(II) in the MeCN/H 2 O solutions used. Additional intermediate products indicate a variety of sulfur oxidation, hydrolysis, and insertion/extrusion reactions forming species that also feed into pathways generating Cu(DTC) 2 .

works.title: Discovery and Engineering of a Flavin‐Containing Monooxygenase From Bradyrhizobium sp. 200 for the Asymmetric Synthesis of an Indoxacarb Intermediate
works.abstract: Indoxacarb is an oxadiazine insecticide bearing a single stereogenic center, of which only the ( S )‐enantiomer exhibits insecticidal activity. Therefore, the synthesis of the key intermediate ( S )‐5‐chloro‐2‐methoxycarbonyl‐2‐hydroxy‐1‐indanone ( 2 ) is crucial for the enantioselective total synthesis of Indoxacarb. In this study, a flavin‐containing monooxygenase from Bradyrhizobium sp. 200 ( Bj FMO) was employed for the asymmetric synthesis of this chiral intermediate, offering a biocatalytic approach as a potential complement to conventional chemical routes. Based on molecular docking and sequence alignment, several amino acid residues located in the FAD and NADPH‐binding domains were selected for site‐saturation mutagenesis. In combination with rational design, additional positions potentially affecting catalytic activity and stability were subjected to site‐directed mutagenesis. Beneficial single mutations were iteratively combined to generate the final variant, Bj FMO M9 . Under optimal conditions, Bj FMO M9 displayed a twofold increase in specific activity compared with the wild type. Its half‐life at 40 °C was extended from 1.3 to 3.0 h, and its tolerance toward isopropanol, ethanol, and acetone was markedly enhanced. In a preparative synthesis, Bj FMO M9 consistently outperformed the wild type, achieving >80% conversion within 10 h and >90% ee for the ( S )‐product.

works.title: Affinity Engineering Modulates Soluble Antigen Degrader Activity
works.abstract: Soluble extracellular proteins drive many physiological and pathological signaling pathways, and targeted degradation offers a potential strategy for their therapeutic modulation. Here, we engineered bispecific targeting chimeras (TACs) that couple soluble proteins to constitutively internalizing cell-surface effectors for clearance. Using transferrin receptor 1 (TfR1) as an initial effector, we find that uptake depends on both binding arms. Rapid target association facilitates extracellular antigen capture, while increased intracellular dissociation can improve uptake when overall binding strength is maintained. Introducing pH-sensitive target binders enhances internalization, but only when neutral-pH affinity remains high. We also find that atypical chemokine receptor 5 (ACKR5) can serve as an alternative internalizing effector. Applying these principles to tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), an optimized TAC more effectively inhibits its signaling than FDA-approved anti-TNF-α therapy adalimumab. These findings identified molecular determinants for engineering TACs targeting soluble extracellular proteins.

works.title: Isolation of Tritonicysteinolic Acid From a Marine Bacterium and Its Evaluation as a PGAM5 Inhibitor
works.abstract: The new sulfolipid-like natural product tritonicysteinolic acid (TTC) was isolated from an extract of the marine bacterium Tritonibacter and exhibited inhibitory activity against PGAM5, a protein phosphatase that localizes in the inner mitochondrial membrane. The full stereochemistry of TTC was elucidated through total synthesis, thereby enabling the synthesis of various derivatives. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies were conducted, which revealed that the derivatives exhibited higher inhibitory activity against PGAM5 phosphatase relative to the parent natural product.

works.title: Alkyl Chain‐Functionalized Nitronyl Nitroxide Radicals: Structure‐Microenvironment Effects on Thiol Kinetics and Dual Antioxidant Behavior
works.abstract: Radical reactivity can be modulated through structural and microenvironmental control, thereby representing an important challenge in the design of redox-active systems. In this study, an alkyl chain-functionalized series of nitronyl nitroxide (NN) radicals designed and synthesized by varying their amphiphilic character. Subsequently, their thiol-based reactivity and microenvironment accessibility, along with antioxidant profile, were investigated. Radical behavior was monitored in aqueous media and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) micelles. Accessibility properties and micellar partitioning of all radicals were evaluated in a concentration-dependent manner, using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). Glutathione (GSH) reactivity and quantitative EPR kinetic analysis revealed that the reduction rate constants systematically decrease with increasing alkyl chain length, leading to the formation of diamagnetic hydroxylamine species. In the presence of SDS, the reactivity of NN derivatives with GSH was dramatically suppressed, confirming the protection of the nitroxide center from thiol reduction. The NN-functionalized derivatives displayed a dual antioxidant mechanism, based on electron transfer and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). The limited superoxide scavenging and pro-oxidant effects indicated radical-specific selectivity under single-electron transfer (SET) conditions. Notably, all derivatives exhibited pronounced inhibition of lipid peroxidation, confirming their effectiveness in chain-breaking antioxidant activity and rendering them competitive agents in targeted therapeutics and stress-based pathologies.

works.title: A DNA Platform‐Assisted Cooperative Probe Addresses the Affinity–Selectivity Trade‐Off in Hybridization‐Based Nucleic Acid Detection at Room Temperature
works.abstract: Hybridization-based nucleic acid detection remains central to molecular diagnostics but is often limited by slow kinetics, diminished sensitivity toward structured or double-stranded targets and low selectivity in recognizing single-nucleotide variation (SNV) at ambient temperatures. Here we introduce a DNA platform-assisted cooperative probe (PCP) that enhances the performance of conventional molecular beacon (MB) probes through cooperative analyte binding mediated by a DNA scaffold. The PCP architecture spatially organizes two analyte-binding arms (F and U) on a dsDNA platform for cooperative tight binding of nucleic acid analytes, which enables the use of a short platform-detached strand m for highly selective SNV recognition. Using clinically relevant targets from Mycoplasma genitalium (23S rRNA fragment) and Neisseria gonorrhoeae (penA gene fragment), we demonstrate that PCP improves SNV selectivity from 10% to 14% for MB probe up to 99%, and lowers the limit of detection by up to an order of magnitude but does not significantly improve hybridization rate. The PCP sensor further enables room-temperature detection of double-stranded polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplicons. These results establish DNA platform-based probe organization as an advantageous strategy to resolve the affinity/specificity trade-off in hybridization-based diagnostics.

works.title: Multienzyme cascades for non-grain carbon feedstocks valorization: Recent advances and perspectives
Enhanced catalytic performance and reusability of ZnO-immobilized pectinase for continuous product yield in food Bioprocessing using response surface methodology
works.abstract: For improved operational stability and reusability, the enzyme was immobilized on zinc oxide nanoparticles. Optimal immobilization was achieved with 2000 U mg−1 pectinase using 2% glutaraldehyde after 150 min of cross-linking at 30 °C. The immobilized enzyme exhibited greater stability across wider pH and temperature. Kinetic analysis indicated that ZnO based immobilization did not cause major effect on the catalytic efficiency of pectinase (Free: 1.017 mg ml−1 min−1 (Km) and 23800 µmol L−1 min−1 (Vmax); Immobilized: 1.116 mg ml−1 min−1 (Km) and 20600 µmol L−1 min−1 (Vmax)). The free and immobilized pectinase was also compared for continuous degradation of pectin, and their yield was compared using response surface methodology (RSM). The contour and 3D plots showed marked difference in performance and stability of free and immobilized enzyme with product yield of 60 mg ml−1 and 180 mg ml−1 for free and immobilized pectinase respectively. These findings suggest that ZnO immobilized pectinase exhibit greater suitability for scale-up in continuous food bioprocessing applications.

works.title: Rumen microbiome carbohydrate metabolism is associated with host lipid metabolic differences between Wagyu and Nanyang cattle
works.abstract: Abstract The rumen microbiome plays an important role in converting dietary carbohydrates into metabolites associated with host physiology, yet the relationships between microbial carbohydrate metabolism and host lipid metabolism remain incompletely understood. Here, we compared Japanese Wagyu and Nanyang cattle to investigate microbiota–metabolite–host associations in relation to breed-associated differences in intramuscular fat (IMF) deposition. Metagenomic analysis revealed differences in rumen microbial community composition and functional profiles between breeds, including differential abundances of carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) families associated with polysaccharide degradation. Wagyu cattle exhibited higher abundances of glycoside hydrolase (GH) families GH5 (cellulose degradation) and GH92 (alpha-mannan degradation), whereas GH13 (starch degradation) and GH43 (arabinoxylan and arabinan degradation) were enriched in Nanyang cattle, together with differences in carbohydrate-degrading genera, including Prevotella , Fibrobacter , and Butyrivibrio . These microbial functional differences were accompanied by distinct fermentation profiles, with higher ruminal acetate and butyrate concentrations in Wagyu cattle and higher propionate concentrations in Nanyang cattle. Proteomic analysis of the longissimus dorsi muscle identified breed-associated differences in proteins involved in lipid synthesis, lipid storage, and energy metabolism, including FABP4, FASN, PLIN1, ACSS2, and IDH1, which showed higher abundances in Wagyu cattle. Correlation analyses identified associations among microbial taxa, CAZyme families, fermentation metabolites, and host proteins related to lipid metabolism and IMF deposition. Overall, these findings reveal coordinated breed-associated differences in rumen microbial functions, fermentation characteristics, and host lipid metabolic profiles, providing insights into microbiota–host metabolic associations related to IMF deposition in cattle. Keypoints • Rumen carbohydrate-active enzyme (CAZyme) profiles differ between Wagyu and Nanyang cattle. • Wagyu cattle show higher acetate and butyrate levels. • Microbiota–volatile fatty acids (VFAs)–proteome axis is linked to intramuscular fat (IMF) deposition

works.title: Numerical analysis of shear rate in a rocking bioreactor and its impact on HL-60 lymphocytes
works.abstract: Abstract The aim of the study was to investigate the influence of hydrodynamic parameters on HL-60 lymphocyte cultures in a rocking disposable bioreactor. A 2D CFD-based model employing the Volume of Fluid (VOF) method was used to characterize the culture microenvironment, while a rotational rheometer was used to determine critical shear thresholds. The developed numerical model was validated against experimental mixing times, yielding an absolute mean percentage difference of 29.2%, demonstrating high predictive accuracy at very low and very high Reynolds numbers, though limitations were observed at medium Reynolds numbers. Results indicated that while averaged shear rates remained below 22.5 s⁻1, local maximum shear rates significantly exceeded the lethal threshold of 1500 s⁻1 for all studied rocking conditions, reaching over 30 000 s⁻1 at the highest parameters. Analysis of shear rate effects on HL-60 lymphocytes demonstrated that cell viability decreases at shear rates higher than 1000 s⁻1 due to cell membrane disruption, up to total disintegration of cells above 1500 s⁻1. The consistent exceeding of these lethal thresholds, particularly during intensified rocking, was shown to negatively impact cell growth and increase the release of intracellular enzymes. Consequently, the successful application of rocking disposable bioreactors for shear-sensitive cultures requires a strategic trade-off between mixing intensification and the mitigation of lethal local shear effects. The developed computational model provides a valuable framework for such optimization and subsequent bioprocess scale-up. Keypoints • 2D CFD VOF model well predicts hydrodynamics in rocking bioreactors. • Local maximum shear rates exceed 1500 s−1 as lethal threshold for HL-60 cells. • Intensification of cell culture requires balanced mixing and hydrodynamic stress.

works.title: An immobilized system with swapping cofactor-recycling enzymes in the synthesis of natural products
works.abstract: Sustainable biosynthesis of small-molecule natural products (NPs) is often hampered by enzyme instability and high cofactor costs. Herein, we developed a modular bi-functional immobilization system to synthesize two NPs (carvone and vanillyl alcohol). Building on the glyoxyl-agarose technology pioneered by Prof. José M. Guisán, we covalently immobilized an alcohol dehydrogenase (BsADH) to allow for biocatalyst reusability. This system was then coupled with two different cofactor-recycling enzymes (LpNOX for NAD + regeneration, and CbFDH for NADH regeneration), which were reversibly immobilized on the same support. The co-immobilization enabled 25–50% higher productivity compared to independently immobilized enzymes. This modular system allows the selective desorption of a cofactor-recycling enzyme (LpNOX, >90% desorption) without affecting the covalently attached ADH, and enabling the co-immobilization of another cofactor-recycling enzyme (CbFDH). This flexible and sustainable platform for redox biocatalysis was applied to the consecutive synthesis of NPs of interest for the pharmaceutical and fragrance industries.

works.title: Visible‐Light‐Triggered Hydroacylation of α ‐Imino Esters With α ‐Keto Esters via Substrate Self‐Catalysis
works.abstract: α ‐Ketoamides are important structural motifs in bioactive molecules. While conceptually efficient, direct acylation of imines toward α ‐ketoamides is hindered by their intrinsic instability and reactivity challenges. Here, we disclose a photochemical hydroacylation of α ‐imino esters with α ‐keto esters that operates without any transition metal or external photosensitizer. Mechanistic elucidation reveals that the α ‐keto ester plays a triple role: It serves as an unconventional hydroacylation donor, a visible‐light absorber, and a hydrogen‐atom abstractor, collectively enabling substrate‐driven self‐catalysis. This strategy provides rapid access to structurally diverse α ‐ketoamide derivatives (44 examples) with high yields (up to 97%) under mild, environmentally benign conditions. By integrating multifunctional substrates and self‐catalytic photoreactivity, this approach expands the toolbox for constructing complex ketoacyl frameworks, offering a concise route toward pharmaceutically relevant motifs.

works.title: Chemoselective Recognition of Vinyl Organometalloids in Cobalt‐Catalyzed Hydrosilylation
works.abstract: Achieving selective functionalization of vinylsilanes in the presence of other terminal C═C bonds remains a significant challenge in organosilicon chemistry. Here, we report a cobalt catalyst supported by a bidentate aminophosphine ligand that enables highly chemoselective hydrosilylation of terminal vinylmetalloids under mild, solvent‐free conditions. The earth‐abundant system operates without external activators, as the hydrosilane substrate itself promotes catalyst activation. Remarkably, reactivity is restricted to terminal vinylmetalloid motifs, encompassing vinylsilanes, vinylgermanes, and vinylboronates, whereas allylsilanes, terminal alkenes, internal alkenes, and 1,1‐disubstituted derivatives remain unreactive. This unusual selectivity enables exclusive transformation of vinylmetalloid groups even in multifunctional substrates containing olefinic sites. Control of substrate stoichiometry further provides access to structurally diverse organosilicon products from multiple‐vinyl precursors with high efficiency.

works.title: Ciprofloxacin Hydrochloride‐Enhanced Potassium tert ‐Butoxide‐Mediated Direct Pyrazinylation of (Hetero)aryl Halides
works.abstract: Aryl pyrazines are increasingly prevalent in the fields of pharmaceuticals and luminescent materials. Base‐promoted cross‐coupling reactions of (hetero)aryl halides with pyrazines can effectively avoid the drawbacks of limited substrate sources in conventional condensation and the cost as well as toxicity issues of noble metal catalysts inherent in transition metal‐catalyzed methods. However, existing methods are predominantly applicable to (hetero)aryl iodides and bromides, whereas the direct use of less reactive (hetero)aryl chlorides remains challenging. Herein, we report a ciprofloxacin hydrochloride with potassium tert ‐butoxide ( t ‐BuOK) catalytic system for the construction of aryl pyrazines. In this reaction, a variety of (hetero)aryl bromides and chlorides prove to be viable substrates and exhibit excellent compatibility with a variety of functional groups. The developed system allows the preparation of aryl pyrazines on a gram‐scale and the functionalization of complex pharmaceuticals. Mechanistic studies reveal that a radical‐mediated pathway is involved in this catalytic transformation.

works.title: Thiolane Sulfoximines as Azide Surrogates for Quinolyl Nitrenes: Photochemical Access to Ortho ‐Diaminoquinolines
works.abstract: Quinolyl nitrenes are valuable reactive intermediates for the synthesis of nitrogen‐containing heterocycles but are commonly generated from hazardous azides under photochemical conditions. Herein, we introduce quinolyl thiolane sulfoximines as practical and thermally stable precursors for the photochemical generation of 8‐quinolyl nitrenes. Upon UV irradiation, these sulfoximines undergo selective S─N bond cleavage and react efficiently with primary and secondary amines, providing direct access to structurally diverse 7,8‐diaminoquinolines in moderate to excellent yields. The transformation releases tetramethylene S‐oxide as a small, benign, readily removable by‐product and exhibits broad functional‐group tolerance, including compatibility with amino acid derivatives, enabling the synthesis of valuable fused δ‐lactam scaffolds. DFT calculations support a mechanism involving nitrene formation followed by azirine trapping and rationalize the experimentally observed selectivity between diaminoquinoline and aminoazepine products. Overall, this work establishes quinolyl sulfoximines as practical and safer surrogates for azides in nitrene photochemistry, providing an efficient platform for the synthesis of 7,8‐diaminoquinolines.

Biotransformation of oleanolic acid using Saccharomyces cerevisiae: New triterpenoids tentatively identified by GC-MS and evaluation of cytotoxic properties
works.abstract: In this context, microbial biotransformation has emerged as an effective, sustainable, and environmentally friendly strategy for generating novel structural derivatives. In the present study, oleanolic acid (OA), one of the most well-known pentacyclic triterpenoids due to its numerous biological activities, was subjected for the first time to biotransformation by Saccharomyces cerevisiae, leading to the formation of new triterpenoid. The analysis of the biotransformation fractions by gas chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (GC-MS), based on the interpretation of fragmentation patterns obtained by electron ionization (EI), enabled the tentative proposal of the structures of seven new triterpenoid derivatives. The spectral data further indicate that these compounds mainly belong to the ∆12-oleanane and ∆12-ursene structural families. The in vitro cytotoxic activity evaluation of all fractions revealed significantly higher activity of the triterpenoid fractions compared to the non-triterpenoid fractions at a concentration of 50 µg/mL. F9 showed significant inhibitory activity against the LS174T cell line (IC50 = 30.5 µg/mL), while F3 showed significant inhibitory activity against the HCT116 cell line (IC50 = 26.4 µg/mL). This study highlights the potential of bioconversion as an eco-friendly strategy for the valorization of valuable natural products, thereby opening the way to new bioactive molecules.

works.title: Programmable bacterial vaccine vectors: A Design–Build–Control framework for precision immune engineering
Next-generation nano-biocatalysts: extremozyme-based nanoparticle system for cypermethrin bioremediation
works.abstract: Abstract Extremozymes, with their exceptional catalytic activity and stability under extreme environmental conditions, have great potential for pesticide remediation. This study involves the isolation and screening of a new extremozyme-producing microbe, Proteus mirabilis JB1, for the production of alkaline-pH-stable laccase. A primary OFAT screening tested a broad range of carbon sources (glucose, lactose, xylose, sucrose, starch, glycerol, cellulose, trisodium citrate, sodium acetate), nitrogen sources (ammonium sulfate, sodium nitrate, urea, beef extract, peptone, casein, gelatin), salts (0.1 mM and 0.01 mM) such as CuSO₄, KCl, ZnCl₂, MgCl₂, MnCl₂, NiCl₂, NaCl, and CaCl₂, and pH levels (7–10). The highest enzyme activity of 0.999 U/ml was achieved using 0.25% (w/v) cellulose, 0.8% (w/v) urea, 0.1 mM MnCl 2 , MgSO 4 , CaCl 2 , NaCl, and KCl, and 0.01 mM CuSO 4 , FeSO 4 , and NiCl 2 at pH 9 with good stability to surfactants (Tween 80, SDS), organic solvents (acetone, ethanol, methanol), and inhibitors (EDTA). PBD and CCD were then implemented to screen and optimize critical parameters—cellulose (1.5% w/v), urea (0.7% w/v), and MgSO₄ (0.05 mM)—to achieve an efficient increase in enzyme activity to 2.3 U/mL, demonstrating the strength and efficacy of the optimization process. Biogenic selenium nanoparticles (Bio-SeNPs) were fabricated and exhibited very high efficiency in pesticide degradation, achieving 100% degradation of cypermethrin without forming any toxic intermediates within 72 h. This research has provided a comprehensive and replicable technique covering microbial isolation, enzyme optimization, fabrication of a nanobiocatalyst, and its application. Key points • A novel isolate, Proteus mirabilis, was employed for the production of the extremozyme laccase. • Optimization increased the yield by 9.58-fold. • Bio-SeNPs were employed to degrade cypermethrin, achieving 100% detoxification within 72 h.

works.title: Colorimetric polymerase spiral reaction (PSR) assay for the rapid detection of hepatitis B virus
works.abstract: Abstract Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a significant global health concern, particularly in low-resource settings with limited access to sophisticated diagnostic tools. Conventional molecular diagnostic assays, such as qPCR, are often restricted to centralized laboratories in urban settings due to their high cost and the need for skilled personnel. This limits its use in lower levels of the healthcare system, highlighting the need for affordable point-of-care (PoC) assays. In this study, we have developed a visual detection method for HBV using a polymerase spiral reaction (PSR) incorporated with hydroxy naphthol blue (HNB) dye. A set of primers was designed targeting a specific region of the S gene of HBV, and the reaction runs in an isothermal condition. The assay conditions were optimized, and the optimal reaction temperature and time were 63 °C and 60 min, respectively. This developed HBV-PSR assay showed a detection limit of 5.04 copies, reaching 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity in clinical evaluation ( n = 85), and colorimetric visualization in 60 min by naked eye. The specificity test revealed no cross-reactivity with other hepatitis-causing viruses and the tested non-HBV pathogens. The assay was tested with 45 HBV-positive clinical samples, which were initially screened by a serological test, and showed a good concordance rate and diagnostic reliability. The HBV-PSR assay designed in this study could potentially be used as a point-of-care diagnostic tool for HBV detection, aiming at early surveillance and detection, focusing on healthcare in poor-resource settings. The combination of isothermal amplification with dye-based visual detection eliminated the need for complex instruments, enabling PoC detection. Key points • A rapid and sensitive PSR assay was developed for HBV detection, with results obtained within 1 h . • HNB dye enabled naked eye visual detection without the need for complex equipment . • The assay detected as few as 5.04 DNA copies and demonstrated high diagnostic performance, outperforming conventional PCR in the evaluated clinical samples .

works.title: Hydrodynamic design space for process transfer across different bioreactor platforms
works.abstract: Abstract The increasing diversification of bioreactor platforms in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, including stirred-tank, 1-D rocking, and orbital-rocking systems, has created challenges for transferring processes across systems with fundamentally different mixing mechanisms. Conventional scale-up parameters, such as power input per unit volume (P/V), are well established for stirred-tank reactors (STRs), but impeller-based methods for estimating P/V are not directly applicable to impeller-free systems. In this study, a computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based framework was developed to define a hydrodynamic design space for process transfer across stirred-tank (STR), 1-D rocking (RM20), and orbital-rocking (CELBIC50) bioreactor systems. Power dissipation per unit volume (Pd/V) was proposed as a platform-independent energy dissipation parameter and combined with shear stress and mixing time to define feasible operating regions. Using this framework, operating conditions could be identified across different bioreactor types using a multi-constraint hydrodynamic design space. Hydrodynamic analysis revealed distinct flow characteristics among the bioreactors, with CELBIC50 exhibiting lower mean shear stress (0.012 vs. 0.019 Pa) and a shorter mixing time (80.9 vs. 146.6 s) than RM20 under the selected operating conditions. Despite these differences, fed-batch CHO cell cultures under the selected conditions showed comparable cell growth, productivity, metabolite profiles, and product quality across STR 2 L, RM20, and CELBIC50, with most performance variables remaining within the common ± 2 σ range. These results demonstrate that a multi-constraint hydrodynamic design space integrating Pd/V, shear stress, and mixing time provides a quantitative framework for identifying transferable operating conditions across different bioreactor systems and supports model-informed process development. Key points • Hydrodynamic characteristics were systematically compared across stirred-tank, 1-D rocking-motion, and orbital-rocking bioreactors under diverse operating conditions. • Pd/V was proposed as a platform-independent energy dissipation parameter across different bioreactor systems. • A constraint-based hydrodynamic design space integrating Pd/V, shear stress, and mixing time was developed for systematic bioprocess transfer.

Operando resolution of CO2 electrolysis interfaces at application-relevant current density reveals water gating
works.abstract: Design of CO2 electroreduction (CO2R) interfaces requires understanding of the dynamic interplay among reactants, surface species and ions. Simplified ideal frameworks, which are conventionally employed to identify these dependencies, provide limited insights under relevant conditions. Here we resolve species interplay in membrane electrode assemblies up to high current densities (1 A cm−2), combining operando Raman spectroscopy and ab initio molecular dynamics. We identify a key role of water ordering in regulation of access to the interface along different operation regimes. Initially, double-layer water exhibits a dominant four-hydrogen-bond (4-HB) coordination with a random configuration. With increasing current density, water rearranges to a three-hydrogen-bond coordination and sits H-down close to the surface, acting as the primary proton source for CO2R and generating adsorbed hydroxides. Eventually, this results in carbonate build-up that increases the concentration of H-down 4-HB water, restricting interface access to COx reactants and promoting hydrogen evolution. These results increase our understanding of CO2R interfaces up to application-relevant current densities. Understanding the dynamic interplay between all components in complex electrocatalytic systems is crucial to advancing their performance. Here operando Raman spectroscopy is used in combination with molecular dynamics simulations to establish the role of water ordering in the mechanism of electrocatalytic CO2 reduction over a range of current densities and under practical conditions.

works.title: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of Vibrio proteolyticus and its postbiotic potential
works.abstract: Abstract Vibrio proteolyticus DCF12.2, isolated from the intestinal tract of the flatfish Dicologlossa cuneata , was characterized through integrated genomic and phenotypic analyses to assess its antimicrobial activity, biosynthetic potential and resistance- and virulence-related features. Genome-based analyses supported its assignment to V. proteolyticus and identified biosynthetic gene clusters associated with arylpolyene, nonribosomal peptide (NRP)-metallophore/amphibactin, ectoine and ribosomally synthesized and posttranslationally modified peptide/nonribosomal peptide synthetase (RiPP-/NRPS)-like pathways, together with numerous predicted antimicrobial peptide candidates. The resistome was mainly composed of chromosomal efflux- and target-associated determinants, whereas virulence-related hits were largely restricted to functions linked to motility, chemotaxis and secretion. The genome also contained sequences homologous to proteins previously described in Photobacterium damselae subsp. piscicida and Vibrio harveyi , as well as three prophage regions and multiple genomic islands (GIs). Phenotypic assays showed that the strain and/or its extracellular products (ECPs) inhibited P. damselae subsp. damselae , V. harveyi and Aeromonas hydrophila . The inhibitory activity of the ECPs against P. damselae subsp. damselae was maintained after incubation at 37 °C and after acidification to pH 5. In conclusion, although the strain exhibits antimicrobial activity and other characteristics that would qualify it a probiotic candidate, the presence of certain virulence factors makes it more suitable for use as a postbiotic. Key points DCF12.2 shows broad genomic potential for antimicrobial compound production Extracellular products inhibit relevant aquatic bacterial pathogens Virulence-related traits support postbiotic rather than probiotic use

works.title: Interkingdom communication 2.0: pheromone-based control between Bacillus subtilis and Saccharomyces cerevisiae
works.abstract: Microbial communities found in nature are complex and thrive in harmony, consisting of organisms derived from several kingdoms. Hence, they need to be able to communicate by quorum-sensing molecules to co-exist in close proximity. Being able to engineer artificial interkingdom communication for biotechnological approaches, such as degradation of complex biomaterials in one fermenter using controlled signaling between microorganisms, would be beneficial. Therefore, we wanted to establish a proof of principle by enabling the Gram-positive bacterium Bacillus subtilis to communicate in a controlled manner with the eukaryotic yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae by exploiting the yeast's pheromone system. We genetically modified B. subtilis to heterologously produce the α-pheromone after bacitracin induction, which in turn would activate the production of the green fluorescent protein mNeongreen upon pheromone recognition by S. cerevisiae. Co-cultivation in modified growth medium and induction of pheromone expression was successful and repeatable. Yeast activation and production of mNeongreen was visible not only by analysis but also by epifluorescence microscopy of the co-culture. This study successfully demonstrated controlled interkingdom signaling between microorganisms by leveraging their native communication systems. KEY POINTS: • Heterologous production and secretion of small peptides in Bacillus subtilis. • Interkingdom communication between bacteria and yeast. • Signaling by artificially produced pheromones.

works.title: Butyrate production from the simultaneous utilization of carbon monoxide and acetate in Eubacterium-dominated enrichments
works.abstract: Abstract Syngas conversion to carboxylic acids can be achieved through the combined actions of acetogens and chain elongators. Mixed cultures enriched with these functional groups can serve as robust and resilient catalysts for bio-based production, but developing efficient and stable communities remains challenging. In this study, we aimed to enrich a mixed microbial culture for efficient syngas-driven chain elongation using carbon monoxide (CO) and acetate as substrates. Three strategies were employed: (i) conventional enrichment using anaerobic sludge only, (ii) sludge augmentation with known syngas fermenters (Clostridium autoethanogenum, Clostridium carboxidivorans, Eubacterium limosum, and Acetobacterium wieringae) to enhance carboxydotrophic activity, and (iii) sludge augmentation with chain elongator Clostridium kluyveri to stimulate chain elongation. Enrichments were performed in batch cultures with stepwise increases in CO partial pressure across successive transfers until a 100% CO (170 kPa) headspace was reached. Ultimately, all enrichments grew under a 100% CO headspace, simultaneously utilizing CO and acetate, with butyrate as main product. 16S rRNA gene and metagenomic analyses revealed that Eubacterium became predominant. Several genera (Aminobacterium, Anaerotignum, Oscillibacter, and Proteiniphilum) not known to ferment CO, were also enriched. Based on physiological and metagenomic analyses, we hypothesize that Eubacterium consumes CO and acetate, producing butyrate and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS)-like material. Metagenomic data further suggests that components derived from this EPS-like material may serve as substrate for the other enriched genera. This study demonstrates that augmentation can steer mixed microbial communities toward targeted product formation and highlights the critical role of initial culture conditions in shaping community composition and functionality. Key points • Mixed cultures converted CO and acetate mainly to butyrate under a 100% CO headspace. • Acetogen augmentation to a mixed community shortened lag-phase in the presence of CO. • Metagenomics suggests microbial use of sugars and amino acids from EPS-like material.

works.title: Effect of enzyme-support interactions on the catalytic behavior of lipases immobilized on magnetic graphene oxide
works.abstract: Understanding enzyme-support interactions is essential for the rational design of immobilized biocatalysts with enhanced activity and stability. This study investigated lipase immobilization by physical adsorption onto graphene oxide modified with superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPION+GO). Five commercial lipases were screened, and Thermomyces lanuginosus lipase (TLL) exhibited the highest specific activity, being selected for further investigation. The immobilized biocatalyst (SPION+GO+TLL) showed 37% higher esterification activity than the free enzyme, together with improved thermal stability and extended half-life. Adsorption promoted favorable enzyme-support interactions that stabilized the active conformation while preserving the flexibility required for catalysis. However, only limited improvements in pH tolerance were observed, indicating that the non-covalent interactions established on the non-functionalized graphene oxide surface were insufficient to ensure enzyme stabilization under different protonation conditions. Opposite catalytic behaviors were also observed under different ethanol hydration conditions: free TLL performed better with hydrated ethanol, whereas the immobilized enzyme was more active in anhydrous ethanol, suggesting that the SPION+GO support created a protective microenvironment for reactions under low-water conditions. These findings demonstrate that enzyme-support interactions, rather than the support itself, govern immobilized lipase performance and provide guidance for developing graphene-based magnetic biocatalysts for biodiesel synthesis and other non-aqueous biocatalytic processes.
